===Dallas Cowboys===
====2010 season====
On April 25, 2010, the [[Dallas Cowboys]] signed Church to a three-year, $1.22 million contract that includes a $3,500 signing bonus after he went undrafted during the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=17 Undrafted Rookies Agree To Terms |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/news.cfm?id=3697FC26-BDDD-E0F1-E1C8D3D4A3B2145F |publisher=Dallascowboys.com |date=April 25, 2010 |accessdate=July 10, 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100428215106/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/news.cfm?id=3697FC26-BDDD-E0F1-E1C8D3D4A3B2145F |archivedate=April 28, 2010 }}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Barry Church contract| url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/jacksonville-jaguars/barry-church-7598/| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Church competed for a roster spot as a backup safety against [[Michael Hamlin]], [[Pat Watkins|Patrick Watkins]], [[Akwasi Owusu-Ansah]], and [[Danny McCray]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Dallas Cowboys Depth Chart: 07/01/2010| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/109/DAL| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Safety the first concern for Dallas Cowboys| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfceast/post/_/id/17215/safety-the-first-concern-for-dallas-cowboys| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=ESPN.com| author=Mosely, Matt| date=August 23, 2010}}</ref> Head coach [[Wade Phillips]] named Church the backup strong safety, behind veteran [[Gerald Sensabaugh]], to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=2010 Cowboys 53-man roster| url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2010/9/4/1670104/2010-cowboys-53-man-roster| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=bloggingtheboys.com| date=September 4, 2010}}</ref>

Church made his NFL debut during Week 2 against the [[2010 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]] after being inactive for their season-opener. He finished 27–20 loss with one assisted tackle. Church made his first career tackle with teammate Danny McCray on [[Danieal Manning]] during a 21-yard kick return by Manning in the second quarter.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 2-2010: Chicago Bears @ Dallas Cowboys| url=https://www.nfl.com/games/bears-at-cowboys-2010-reg-2| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> During Week 8, Church collected a season-high four combined tackles during a 35–17 loss to the [[2010 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]]. On November 9, 2010, the Cowboys fired head coach Wade Phillips after a 45–7 road loss to the [[2010 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] and falling to a 1–7 record.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watkins |first=Calvin |date=November 9, 2010 |title=Cowboys' Wade Phillips fired |url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nfl/news/story?id=5780262 |access-date=March 26, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Church finished his rookie season with 20 combined tackles (15 solo) in 15 games and no starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Barry Church (career)| url=https://www.nfl.com/players/barry-church/stats/career| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished fourth on the team with 16 tackles on [[special teams]].

====2011 season====
Church returned to training camp in 2011 and competed for a role as a backup safety against [[Andrew Sendejo]], Danny McCray, Akwasi Owusu-Ansah, and Michael Hamlin. New head coach [[Jason Garrett]] named him the backup behind Gerald Sensabaugh and [[Abram Elam]] to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Dallas Cowboys Depth Chart: 09/04/2011| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/123/DAL| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=A Complete Look At The 2011 Dallas Cowboys Roster| url=https://dallas.sbnation.com/2011/9/4/2404636/dallas-cowboys-roster-2011| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=dallas.sbnation.com| author=Perryman, Brett| date=September 4, 2011}}</ref>

During Week 4, Church recorded a season-high six combined tackles in a 34–30 loss to the [[2011 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]]. On December 11, 2011, he earned his first NFL start and recorded two solo tackles before leaving the eventual 37–34 loss to the [[2011 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] in the third quarter with a shoulder injury. Church was placed on injured reserve two days later after discovering his shoulder would require surgery to repair the [[Acromioclavicular joint|AC joint]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Cowboys sign safety, Barry Church to IR| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4688106/cowboys-sign-safety-barry-church-to-ir| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=ESPN.com| author=Archer, Todd| date=December 13, 2011}}</ref>

Church finished his second professional season with 28 combined tackles (21 solo) in 13 games and one start.<ref name="career"/>

====2012 season====
After two seasons of increasing playing time as a hybrid linebacker and safety, Church returned to training camp and competed for the job as the starting strong safety against [[Brodney Pool]]. Church was named the starting strong safety, alongside free safety Gerald Sensabaugh, to start season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Dallas Cowboys Depth Chart: 09/01/2012| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/135/DAL | accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

Church started the season-opener at the [[2012 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] and recorded two combined tackles in a 24–17 victory. Two weeks later, he made a season-high three solo tackles in a 16–10 victory over the [[2012 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], but left in the third quarter after sustaining a torn Achilles. He underwent surgery to repair the tendon two days later.<ref>{{cite web| title=Barry Church undergoes Achilles surgery| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4698368/barry-church-undergoes-surgery-on-his-achilles| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=ESPN.com| author=Watkins, Calvin| date=September 25, 2012}}</ref> Church finished his last season under defensive coordinator [[Rob Ryan]] with six combined tackles (four solo) in three games and three starts.<ref name="career"/>

Still rehabbing from a serious injury, the Cowboys took a gamble that Church would make a full recovery and on October 26, 2012, signed him to a four-year, $8.82 million contract extension that included $3.32 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $2.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapoport |first=Ian |author-link=Ian Rapoport |date=October 26, 2012 |title=Barry Church, Dallas Cowboys sign four-year contract extension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/barry-church-dallas-cowboys-sign-four-year-contract-extension-0ap1000000085662 |access-date=March 26, 2018 |website=[[National Football League]]}}</ref>

====2013 season====
Throughout training camp, Church competed for the job as the starting free safety against rookie [[J. J. Wilcox]] and [[Matt Johnson (safety)|Matt Johnson]] after it was left vacant by the retirement of [[Gerald Sensabaugh]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Cowboys rookie safety J.J. Wilcox showing his physicality even without pads on| url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-cowboys/cowboysheadlines/2013/05/11/cowboys-rookie-safety-j.j.-wilcox-showing-his-physicality-even-without-pads-on| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=sportsday.dallasnews.com| author=Machota, John| date=May 21, 2013}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Defensive coordinator [[Monte Kiffin]] named him the starting free safety, along with strong safety [[Will Allen (safety)|Will Allen]], to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Dallas Cowboys Depth Chart: 09/05/2013| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/DAL | accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On October 20, 2013, Church recorded five combined tackles, broke up a pass, and made his first NFL interception off quarterback [[Matt Barkley]] during a 17–3 road victory over the [[2013 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]]. During Week 10, he collected a season-high 14 combined tackles (nine solo) in a 49–17 road loss to the [[2013 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]]. Two weeks later, Church made 13 combined tackles (eight solo) in a 24–21 road victory over the [[2013 New York Giants season|New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Barry Church (2013)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/barrychurch/494259/gamelogs?season=2013| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> When injuries impacted the depth at linebacker, he also provided help by playing linebacker on passing situations. Church finished his first full season as a starter leading the team with 147 combined tackles (107 solo), six pass deflections, three forced fumbles (led the team), and an interception in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2014 season====
Church entered training camp slated as the starting free safety with starting strong safety J.J. Wilcox.<ref>{{cite web| title=Position Battle: Big Safety Competition Opposite Church| url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/position-battle-big-safety-competition-opposite-church-350471| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=dallascowboys.com| date=July 7, 2014}}</ref> During Week 12, Church recorded eight solo tackles, deflected a pass, and returned an interception by [[Eli Manning]] for a 45-yard gain during a 35–28 road victory over the [[2014 New York Giants season|New York Giants]]. In the next game, he collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (nine solo) and broke up a pass in a 33–10 loss to the [[2014 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref name="stats14">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Barry Church (2014)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/barrychurch/494259/gamelogs?season=2014| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> Church led the team with 110 combined tackles (77 solo), six pass deflections, two interceptions, and a forced fumble in 16 starts.<ref name="career"/>

The Cowboys finished atop the [[NFC East]] with a 12–4 record and received a playoff berth. On January 4, 2015, Church started in his first NFL playoff game and recorded four combined tackles during a 24–20 victory against the [[2014 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] in the NFC Wildcard Game. The following week, he made eight combined tackles during the 26–21 road loss to the [[2014 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] in the NFL Divisional Game.<ref name="stats14"/>

====2015 season====
Defensive coordinator [[Rod Marinelli]] opted to retain Church and Wilcox as the starting safety duo after assistant head coach/co-defensive coordinator Monte Kiffin was not re-signed during the off-season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Report: Monte Kiffin will not return to the Cowboys' coaching staff| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2015/02/10/dallas-cowboys-monte-kiffin-leaving-coaching-staff| accessdate=March 26, 2018| website=si.com| date=February 10, 2015}}</ref>

During a Week 10 10–6 road loss to the [[2015 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Church collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (nine solo). On December 13, 2015, he tied his season-high of 11 combined tackles (nine solo) during a 28–7 loss at the [[2015 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]]. Two weeks later against the [[2015 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]], Church recorded seven combined tackles, but left the eventual 16–6 road loss in the fourth quarter after breaking his arm.<ref>{{cite web| title=Cowboys injury report: Barry Church headed to IR, Devin Street has a concussion| url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-cowboys/cowboys/2015/12/28/cowboys-injury-report-barry-church-headed-ir-devin-street-concussion| accessdate=March 27, 2018| website =sportsday.dallasnews.com| author=Machota, John| date=December 27, 2015}}</ref> He was expected to be in a cast for 6–8 weeks and missed the regular-season finale.<ref>{{cite web| title=Barry Church Suffers Broken Arm, Expects 6-To-8 Week Recovery Time| url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/barry-church-suffers-broken-arm-expects-6-to-8-week-recovery-time-396931| accessdate=March 27, 2018| website=Dallascowboys.com| author=Helman, David| date=December 27, 2015}}</ref> Church finished second on the team with 136 combined tackles (78 solo) and a forced fumble in 15 games and starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2016 season====
Head coach [[Jason Garrett]] named Church the starting strong safety, alongside starting free safety [[Byron Jones (American football)|Byron Jones]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Dallas Cowboys Depth Chart: 09/01/2016| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/123/DAL | accessdate=March 27, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

During a Week 2 27–23 road victory over the [[2016 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]], Church made five combined tackles, broke up a pass, and intercepted a pass by [[Kirk Cousins]] in the endzone. The interception set up the Cowboys' game-winning drive.<ref>{{cite web|title=Morris' TD after Cousins' INT leads Cowboys past Skins 27–23|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=400874518|website=ESPN.com|date=March 9, 2017}}</ref> During a Week 6 30–16 road victory over the [[2016 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]], Church had five tackles, a forced fumble, a pass defended, and a third-quarter interception. Two weeks later against the [[2016 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], he made three combined tackles before leaving the eventual 29–23 victory in the third quarter after fracturing his forearm during a touchdown drive by the Eagles. He was sidelined for four consecutive games (Weeks 9–12) due to the injury, but returned in Week 13 and opted to play with a cast on.<ref>{{cite web| title=Cowboys safety Barry Church, cornerback Mo Claiborne both suffer injuries in second half| url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-cowboys/cowboys/2016/10/30/cowboys-db-barry-church-taken-locker-room-evaluated-arm-injury| accessdate=March 27, 2018| website=sportsday.dallasnews.com}}</ref>

During a Week 16 42–21 victory over the [[2016 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]], Church collected a season-high 12 combined tackles (seven solo).<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Barry Church (2016)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/barrychurch/494259/gamelogs?season=2016| accessdate=March 27, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the 2016 season with 85 combined tackles (61 solo), four passes defended, and two interceptions in 12 games and starts.<ref name="career"/> Church received an overall grade of 86.2 from Pro Football Focus in 2016 and ranked ninth among all qualifying safeties.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ranking all 32 NFL secondaries this season| url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/news/pro-ranking-all-32-nfl-secondaries-this-season| accessdate=March 27, 2018| website=profootballfocus.com| author=Claasen, Matt| date=January 10, 2017}}</ref>

The Cowboys finished atop the [[NFC East]] with a 13–3 record and received a first-round bye. In the Divisional Round against the [[2016 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]], Church made four combined tackles and made his first NFL sack on [[Aaron Rodgers]] as the Cowboys narrowly lost by a score of 34–31.

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On March 9, 2017, the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] signed Church to a four-year, $26 million contract that includes $12 million guaranteed.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars expected to land safety Barry Church|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jaguars-expected-to-land-safety-barry-church-0ap3000000791514|author=Patra, Kevin|website=NFL.com|date=March 9, 2017|accessdate=March 27, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-barry-church-signs-with-jaguars-18637304|title=OFFICIAL: Barry Church signs with Jaguars|work=Jaguars.com|date=March 10, 2017|first= John|last= Oehser }}</ref> Head coach [[Doug Marrone]] named Church the starting strong safety, along with free safety [[Tashaun Gipson]], after it was left vacant due to [[Johnathan Cyprien]]'s departure to the [[Tennessee Titans]] in free agency.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Jacksonville Jaguars Depth Chart: 09/02/2017| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/199/JAX| accessdate=March 27, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

====2017 season====
During a Week 4 23–20 road loss to the [[2017 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], Church made six combined tackles and sacked quarterback [[Josh McCown]] once. In the next game, Church recorded five combined tackles, deflected a pass, and returned an interception by [[Ben Roethlisberger]] for a 51-yard touchdown during a 30–9 road victory over the [[2017 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]]. It marked his second touchdown in eight seasons. The Jaguars' defense set a franchise record by intercepting five passes by Roethlisberger during their game. During a Week 12 27–24 road loss to the [[2017 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]], he collected a season-high nine combined tackles, broke up a pass, and intercepted a pass by [[Carson Palmer]].

Church finished his first season with the Jaguars with 72 combined tackles (58 solo), eight pass deflections, four interceptions, 1.5 sacks, and a touchdown in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career"/> The Jaguars finished atop the [[AFC South]] with a 10–6 record to clinch a playoff berth. They defeated the [[2017 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] by a score of 10–3 in the AFC Wildcard Game and went on to narrowly defeat the Steelers on the road 45–42 in the AFC Divisional round. Church recorded seven combined tackles in the game against the Steelers. On January 21, 2018, Church made a tackle during a 24–20 loss on the road against the [[2017 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]]. He drew criticism and received a personal foul after delivering a hit to tight end [[Rob Gronkowski]]'s head during the second quarter. Gronkowski did not return after he suffered a [[concussion]]. On January 26, 2018, Church was fined $24,309 for the hit.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 26, 2018 |title=Barry Church fined $24,309 for hit on Rob Gronkowski |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/barry-church-fined-24-309-for-hit-on-rob-gronkowski-0ap3000000911327 |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave Church an overall grade of 83.2 in 2017, ranking him 22nd among all qualifying safeties.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: Barry Church| url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/barry-church/5924| accessdate=March 27, 2018| website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

====2018 season====
Church entered the 2018 season slated as the starting strong safety alongside free safety [[Tashaun Gipson]]. He started the first 11 games, but was benched in Weeks 13 and 14 in favor of rookie [[Ronnie Harrison]] due to mistakes in pass coverage. On December 14, 2018, Church was released after officially losing the starting job.<ref>{{Cite news |last=DiRocco |first=Michael |date=December 14, 2018 |title=After losing starting spot, safety Barry Church released by Jaguars |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/25535483/jacksonville-jaguars-release-safety-barry-church |access-date=2025-01-06 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 14, 2018 |title=Jaguars make roster moves |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-roster-moves-x8832 |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He finished the 2018 season with 38 tackles (32 solo), a sack, an interception, and two passes defended.

'''Barrett A. Jones''' (born May 25, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] as a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], winning the [[Rimington Trophy]] as the best center in college football. He was selected by the [[St. Louis Rams]] in the fourth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/prospectrankings/TSX/2013_OG |title=2013 OG Draft Prospects |work=CBS Sports |access-date=July 21, 2010}}</ref>

==Early life==
Jones was born in [[Memphis, Tennessee]].  He attended [[Evangelical Christian School]] in Memphis, where he played for the Evangelical Christian Eagles [[high school football]] team.  Following his senior season in 2007, he was a first-team all-state selection by ''[[The Tennessean]]'' and the Tennessee Sports Writers Association, and was a U.S. Army high school All-American.

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Barrett-Jones-54227;_ylt=AjpS6TaCokLMD6VnCFIHjBdDPZB4|title=Rivals.com|website=sports.yahoo.com}}</ref> Jones was listed as the No. 1 center in the nation in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-1827/0|title=Rivals.com|website=sports.yahoo.com}}</ref>

His father Rex attended the University of Alabama and played for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball]] team from 1982 to 1984.
Barrett has two brothers, Harrison and Walker, that also played football for the University of Alabama. Barrett's grandfather, [[Bill Jones (basketball, born 1936)|Bill Jones]], is a college basketball head coaching legend in the state of Alabama.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wray |first=Cheryl |date=2013-05-17 |title=UNA legend (and Barrett's grandfather) Bill Jones earns induction into the Alabama Sports Hall of Fame |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2013/05/una_legend_and_barretts_grandf.html |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=AL.com |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Barrett Jones 2011.jpg|thumb|left|250px|upright=3.|Jones at Alabama circa 2011.]]
Jones received an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Alabama]], where he played for coach [[Nick Saban]]'s [[Alabama Crimson Tide football team]] from [[2008 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|2008]] to [[2012 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|2012]].  After [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his initial year at Alabama, Jones started all 14 games for [[2009 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama's 2009 national championship team]] at right guard. He subsequently earned Freshman All-America honors from ''[[College Football News]]'' and Phil Steele.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://alabama.scout.com/2/927604.html |title=Barrett Jones Is Frosh All-America |work=BamaMag.com |date=December 9, 2009 |access-date=July 21, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716165638/http://alabama.scout.com/2/927604.html |archive-date=July 16, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In his junior season, because of team needs, he switched from guard to left tackle where he started all 13 games for another [[2011 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama national championship team]].  Following his 2011 junior season, he was a first-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) selection, and was recognized as a unanimous first-team All-American.  He was the winner of the 2011 Outland Trophy given to the best lineman in college football.  In his senior year, again because of team needs, he switched from tackle to center.  He started every game at center for the team that won another National Championship in 2012.  He did not receive a second Outland Trophy but won the Rimington Trophy given each year to the outstanding college center becoming only the 2nd person in history to win both an Outland and a Rimington.  He is the only person to win an Outland and a Rimington at two different positions or in two different years. Barrett Jones ended his Alabama career winning 3 BCS National Championships—each Championship at a different position—as an All-American guard, an All-American right tackle and an All-American center.

Off the field, he has earned a degree in accounting, graduating ''[[summa cum laude]]'' in August 2011 with a 4.0 grade point average.  He graduated in December 2012 with his masters again maintaining a 4.0 GPA.  In addition, he was honored as one of 11 members of the 2011 Allstate AFCA Good Work "which honors football student-athletes for exemplary community service."  Jones won the 2012 [[William V. Campbell Trophy]], an award given by the National Football Foundation & College Hall of Fame to college's football's "best and brightest."  He is a 2010 and 2011 Academic All-American and in his final school year of 2012–13, he earned distinction as both the [[Division I (NCAA)|NCAA Division I]] [[List of Football Academic All-America Team Members of the Year|Football Academic All-America Team Member of the Year]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cosida.com/news.aspx?id=3901|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130110191458/http://cosida.com/news.aspx?id=3901|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 10, 2013|title=Alabama's Barrett Jones tops Capital One Academic All-America® Division I Football Team|access-date=December 6, 2012|date=December 6, 2012|publisher=[[College Sports Information Directors of America]]}}</ref> and the [[List of Academic All-America Team Members of the Year|Academic All-America Team Member of the Year]] for all NCAA Division I sports.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.cosida.com/news.aspx?id=4172|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130810013728/http://www.cosida.com/news.aspx?id=4172|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 10, 2013|title=Barrett Jones of Alabama named Capital One Division I Academic All-America® of the Year|date=August 8, 2013|access-date=November 19, 2013|publisher=[[College Sports Information Directors of America]]}}</ref> He received the 2011 ARA Sportsmanship Award and  2011 Wuerffel Trophy for combined athletic, academic and community service achievement. On December 6, 2012, Jones was awarded the [[Rimington Trophy]] as the best center in college football.<ref name=Rimington>{{cite news|last=Kausler, Jr.|first=Don|title=Alabama's Barrett Jones wins the 2012 Rimington Trophy as the nation's best center|url=http://www.al.com/alabamafootball/index.ssf/2012/12/alabamas_barrett_jones_wins_th.html|access-date=December 6, 2012|date=December 6, 2012|agency=AL.com}}</ref> Finally, he was named one of the 2014 recipients of the [[Today's Top 10 Award]], given annually by the NCAA to 10 outstanding student-athletes who graduated in the school year before the award presentation.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-selects-today%E2%80%99s-top-10-2014 |title=NCAA selects Today's Top 10 for 2014 |publisher=NCAA |date=November 8, 2013 |access-date=January 27, 2014}}</ref>

Jones suffered a serious foot injury in the first quarter of the SEC Championship game but played the entire game so well that his teammates did not even know he had been injured.  Even with the injury, in the BCS Championship game four weeks later, Jones earned praise for handling [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]] nose tackle [[Louis Nix III]] mostly by himself, giving left guard [[Chance Warmack]] the freedom to maneuver downfield to block Fighting Irish linebackers for [[Eddie Lacy]] and [[T. J. Yeldon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/blog/rob-rang/21512472/nfl-draft-bcs-title-game-observations|title=NCAA Football News}}</ref> After the game, he announced that he had a [[Lisfranc injury]] of the left foot with at least 2 torn ligaments.<ref name="k342">{{cite web | last=Low | first=Chris | title=Alabama C Jones had injured foot in title game | website=ESPN.com | date=2013-01-08 | url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/bowls12/story/_/id/8823901/alabama-crimson-tide-center-barrett-jones-played-bcs-national-championship-injured-foot | access-date=2025-01-06}}</ref>   He was scheduled for surgery immediately upon returning home to Alabama. As a result, he was unable to participate in the [[NFL Scouting Combine|NFL Combine]].

===St. Louis Rams===
In the [[2013 NFL draft]], Jones was selected by the [[St. Louis Rams]] in the fourth round with the 113th overall draft pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He participated in ten games from 2013 to 2014. On September 5, 2015, he was waived by the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Reduce Roster to 53 Players|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Reduce-Roster-to-53-Players/bbb8735b-9b5a-4007-ae0f-b8e4cf251956|author=Simmons, Myles|website=TheRams.com|date=September 5, 2015|access-date=April 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170412061334/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Reduce-Roster-to-53-Players/bbb8735b-9b5a-4007-ae0f-b8e4cf251956|archive-date=April 12, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On September 8, 2015, Jones was signed to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]' practice squad. On September 29, 2015, he was released from practice squad.

===Chicago Bears===
On October 6, 2015, Jones was signed by the [[Chicago Bears]]' practice squad, following a season-ending injury to [[Will Montgomery]].

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On November 30, 2015, Jones was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] from the Bears' practice squad. ===Washington Redskins===
Rambo was selected by the [[Washington Redskins]] in the sixth round (191st overall) of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jones |first=Mike |date=April 27, 2013 |title=Redskins take another safety, Bacarri Rambo, with 191st overall pick |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2013/04/27/redskins-take-another-safety-bacarri-rambo-with-191st-overall-pick/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130429045431/http://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2013/04/27/redskins-take-another-safety-bacarri-rambo-with-191st-overall-pick/ |archive-date=April 29, 2013 |access-date=April 29, 2013 |work=The Washington Post}}</ref> He signed a four-year contract worth roughly $430,788 per year on May 13, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tinsman |first=Brian |date=May 13, 2013 |title=Redskins Sign Draft Picks Rambo, Jenkins |url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Draft-Picks-Rambo-Jenkins/b23c9975-68c0-4e0b-934f-74532a157c5b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607090243/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Draft-Picks-Rambo-Jenkins/b23c9975-68c0-4e0b-934f-74532a157c5b |archive-date=June 7, 2013 |access-date=May 14, 2013 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=McMillan |first=Keith |date=May 13, 2013 |title=Redskins sign Rambo, Jenkins; five rookie draftees still unsigned |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2013/05/13/redskins-sign-rambo-jenkins-five-rookie-draftees-still-unsigned/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130513221148/http://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2013/05/13/redskins-sign-rambo-jenkins-five-rookie-draftees-still-unsigned/ |archive-date=May 13, 2013 |access-date=May 14, 2013 |work=WashingtonPost.com}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills (first stint)===
Rambo signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] on November 17, 2014, after the Bills had placed cornerback [[Leodis McKelvin]] on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=November 17, 2014 |title=Bills sign Bacarri Rambo, place Leodis McKelvin on injured reserve |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/17/bills-sign-bacarri-rambo-place-leodis-mckelvin-on-injured-reserve/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141119191316/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/17/bills-sign-bacarri-rambo-place-leodis-mckelvin-on-injured-reserve/ |archive-date=November 19, 2014 |access-date=November 17, 2014 |website=ProFootballTalk}}</ref> Rambo had two interceptions off of [[2014 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] quarterback [[Aaron Rodgers]] on December 14, 2014, in Week 15.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Buffalo Bills – December 14th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201412140buf.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230516221346/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201412140buf.htm |archive-date=May 16, 2023 |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He appeared in six games in the 2014 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bacarri Rambo 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RambBa00/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710192241/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RambBa00/gamelog/2014/ |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

On November 12, 2015, Rambo contributed significantly during a Thursday night win against the [[2015 New York Jets season|New York Jets]]. Rambo forced two fumbles, one of which was returned by [[Duke Williams (safety)|Duke Williams]] for a touchdown, the other recovered by Rambo himself.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at New York Jets – November 12th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511120nyj.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119120157/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511120nyj.htm |archive-date=January 19, 2018 |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Rambo also had the game-sealing interception off of [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]] with less than a minute remaining in the 22–17 win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ferrara |first=Kyle |date=November 13, 2015 |title=Bacarri Rambo makes big impact in big Bills win |url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bacarri-Rambo-makes-big-impact-in-big-Bills-win/fea6ab50-c19e-4c2b-9798-6317d5ab58d6 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218174419/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bacarri-Rambo-makes-big-impact-in-big-Bills-win/fea6ab50-c19e-4c2b-9798-6317d5ab58d6 |archive-date=December 18, 2015 |access-date=April 17, 2016 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref> As a result of his performance in Week 10, Rambo was named as the AFC Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=November 18, 2015 |title=Bacarri Rambo named AFC defensive player of the week |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bacarri-rambo-named-afc-defensive-player-of-the-week |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119060340/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/11/18/bacarri-rambo-named-afc-defensive-player-of-the-week/ |archive-date=November 19, 2015 |access-date=February 24, 2025 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He appeared in 15 games and started eight in the 2015 season. He recorded one sack, 62 total tackles, one interception, six passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bacarri Rambo 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RambBa00/gamelog/2015/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710192241/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RambBa00/gamelog/2015/ |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He became a free agent at the end of the season.

===Miami Dolphins===
On October 25, 2016, Rambo was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=October 25, 2016 |title=Dolphins Signing S Bacarri Rambo |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/dolphins-signing-s-bacarri-rambo/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710191430/https://nfltraderumors.co/dolphins-signing-s-bacarri-rambo/ |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref> In the Week 14 win over the [[2016 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]], he recorded his fourth career interception against quarterback [[Carson Palmer]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Congemi |first=John |date=December 12, 2016 |title=Three Takeaways From The Cardinals Game |url=http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-4/Three-Takeaways-From-The-Cardinals-Game/0f54bffc-a5af-4fe6-b20f-8b2b04a6dbef |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221163557/http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-4/Three-Takeaways-From-The-Cardinals-Game/0f54bffc-a5af-4fe6-b20f-8b2b04a6dbef |archive-date=December 21, 2016 |access-date=December 21, 2016 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> He appeared in nine games and started five in the 2016 season. '''Barkevious Leon Mingo''' ({{IPAc-en|b|ɑr|ˈ|k|iː|v|i|ə|s}}; born October 4, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]] (LSU) and was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] sixth overall in the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He won [[Super Bowl LI]] with the [[New England Patriots]].

==Early life==
Mingo was born in [[Belle Glade, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saint Thomas Aquinas High School of Fort Lauderdale Has Most NFL Players |url=https://nflcommunications.com/Pages/Saint-Thomas-Aquinas-High-School-of-Fort-Lauderdale-Has-Most-NFL-Players--.aspx |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=NFL Communications |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710190614/https://nflcommunications.com/Pages/Saint-Thomas-Aquinas-High-School-of-Fort-Lauderdale-Has-Most-NFL-Players--.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref> He attended [[West Monroe High School]] in [[West Monroe, Louisiana]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 24, 2013 |title=Why We Love Football: Barkevious Mingo |url=https://clevelandmagazine.com/in-the-cle/sports/articles/why-we-love-football-barkevious-mingo |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=Cleveland Magazine |language=en |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710190700/https://clevelandmagazine.com/in-the-cle/sports/articles/why-we-love-football-barkevious-mingo |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Barkevious Mingo, 2009 Outside Linebacker, Louisiana State |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/barkevious-mingo-28540?view=pv |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US |archive-date=July 15, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715015339/https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/barkevious-mingo-28540?view=pv |url-status=live }}</ref> where he was a letterman in football and track. He played [[high school football|football]] for the West Monroe Rebels team under head coach [[Don Shows]]. As a junior, he tallied 55 tackles to go with six sacks and 12 tackles for loss, leading this to be named All-State in Class 5A. As a senior in 2008, he was a 5A first-team All-state selection, after recording 59 tackles to go with seven tackles for loss and four sacks in helping lead West Monroe High School to the state championship game. He also added four forced fumbles and recovered seven fumbles. He played in the 2009 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 7, 2013 |title=Tennessee-based 247Sports signs on as partner for the U.S. Army All-American Bowl |url=http://www.knoxnews.com/sports/vols/football/tennessee-based-247sports-signs-on-as-partner-for-the-us-army-all-american-bowl-ep-358337277-355877621.html |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=Knoxville News Sentinel |language=en |archive-date=July 15, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715015357/https://archive.knoxnews.com/sports/vols/football/tennessee-based-247sports-signs-on-as-partner-for-the-us-army-all-american-bowl-ep-358337277-355877621.html/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Also a standout [[track & field]] athlete, Mingo was a state qualifier as a [[sprint (running)|sprinter]]. At the 2008 Region I-5A Meet, he took gold in the [[400-meter dash]], with a PR of 48.92, and ran the lead leg on the West Monroe [[4 × 200 metres relay|4 × 200m]] and [[4 × 400 metres relay|4 × 400m]] squads, helping them capture the state title in both events.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Louisiana Milesplit |url=https://la.milesplit.com/ |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=MileSplit United States |language=en |archive-date=July 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703042712/https://la.milesplit.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref> At the 2009 LHSAA Outdoor State T&F Championships, he took 5th in the [[200-meter dash]], recording a career-best time of 21.85 seconds, and finished 6th in the 400-meter dash, with a time of 49.54 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LHSAA Outdoor State Championships 2009 - 3A, 4A, & 5A (Raw) |url=https://la.milesplit.com/meets/55027-lhsaa-outdoor-state-championships-2009/results/93663/raw |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=Louisiana Milesplit |language=en |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710190916/https://la.milesplit.com/meets/55027-lhsaa-outdoor-state-championships-2009/results/93663/raw |url-status=live }}</ref>

According to ''[[Rivals.com]]'' and ''[[Scout.com]]'', Mingo was four-star college recruiting prospect.<ref name="ohio">{{Cite web |title=Barkevious Mingo |url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=3660186 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130821175541/http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=3660186 |archive-date=August 21, 2013 |access-date=October 26, 2014 |website=LSUSports.net}}</ref> He was rated as the No. 6 strong side linebacker by Scout.com and the No. 9 by Rivals.com. He was a member of the Rivals 250 and Scout 300. He was rated as the No. 5 best athlete among linebackers by Rivals.com. He was rated as the No. 3 player in the state of [[Louisiana]] by SuperPrep and the No. 8 by Rivals.com.

===Cleveland Browns===
====2013====
Mingo was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the first round with the sixth overall pick in the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=April 25, 2013 |title=Barkevious Mingo drafted by Cleveland Browns |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/barkevious-mingo-drafted-by-cleveland-browns-0ap1000000163391 |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710185549/https://www.nfl.com/news/barkevious-mingo-drafted-by-cleveland-browns-0ap1000000163391 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was the third defensive end to be selected in the draft, after [[Dion Jordan]] and [[Ezekiel Ansah]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002095516/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>
{{external media 
| video1 =
[http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-draft/0ap2000000163566/Browns-draft-Barkevious-Mingo-No-6 Browns draft Barkevious Mingo sixth overall]
}}

On July 21, 2013, the Browns signed Mingo to a four-year, $16.34 million contract that included a [[signing bonus]] of $10.26 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 21, 2013 |title=Barkevious Mingo Signs Rookie Contract With Browns |url=https://www.dawgsbynature.com/2013/7/21/4543058/barkevious-mingo-signs-rookie-contract-with-browns |access-date=January 2, 2019 |website=Dawgs By Nature |archive-date=January 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103055821/https://www.dawgsbynature.com/2013/7/21/4543058/barkevious-mingo-signs-rookie-contract-with-browns |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Barkevious Mingo contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/barkevious-mingo-12286/ |access-date=January 2, 2019 |website=Spotrac.com |archive-date=January 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103060235/https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/barkevious-mingo-12286/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Mingo was immediately moved to outside linebacker by defensive coordinator [[Ray Horton]] and competed against [[Jabaal Sheard]] for a starting role throughout training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 11, 2013 |title=Cleveland Browns linebacker Barkevious Mingo continues to impress with his athleticism (Browns notes) |url=https://www.morningjournal.com/news/cleveland-browns-linebacker-barkevious-mingo-continues-to-impress-with-his/article_3a6600af-7daf-508b-943b-088df86045d7.html |access-date=January 2, 2019 |website=MorningJournal.com |archive-date=January 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103005048/https://www.morningjournal.com/news/cleveland-browns-linebacker-barkevious-mingo-continues-to-impress-with-his/article_3a6600af-7daf-508b-943b-088df86045d7.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On August 15, 2013, Mingo suffered a bruised lung during the Browns' 24–6 win against the [[2013 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] during their second preseason game. Mingo was hospitalized and missed the last two games of the preseason.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hanzus |first=Dan |date=August 15, 2013 |title=Barkevious Lunt and recorded Mingo hospitalized with bruised lung |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/barkevious-mingo-might-miss-1-week-with-bruised-lung-0ap1000000230472 |access-date=August 15, 2013 |website=[[NFL.com]] |archive-date=August 18, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130818012928/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000230472/article/barkevious-mingo-hospitalized-with-bruised-lung |url-status=live }}</ref> Head coach [[Rob Chudzinski]] named Mingo a backup outside linebacker, behind Sheard and  [[Paul Kruger (American football)|Paul Kruger]], to begin the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hangst |first=Andrea |date=August 26, 2013 |title=Cleveland Browns Roster 2013: Latest Cuts, Depth Charts and Analysis |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1751060-cleveland-browns-roster-2013-latest-cuts-depth-charts-and-analysis |access-date=January 2, 2019 |website=Bleacher Report |archive-date=April 4, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404101801/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1751060-cleveland-browns-roster-2013-latest-cuts-depth-charts-and-analysis |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 15, [[2013 Cleveland Browns season|2013]], Mingo made his professional regular season debut after missing the season opener due to a bruised lung and recorded two solo tackles, one pass deflection, and made his first career sack during their 14–6 loss at the [[2013 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]] in Week 2. On March 16, 2018, the [[Seattle Seahawks]] signed Mingo to a two-year, $6.80 million contract that includes $3.20 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $2.20 million.<ref name="spotrac" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=March 14, 2018 |title=Seahawks add Barkevious Mingo |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/14/seahawks-add-barkevious-mingo/ |access-date=March 14, 2018 |website=NBCSports.com |archive-date=March 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315133929/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/14/seahawks-add-barkevious-mingo/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=March 16, 2018 |title=Seahawks Sign Linebacker Barkevious Mingo |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2018/03/16/seahawks-sign-linebacker-barkevious-mingo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318120657/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2018/03/16/seahawks-sign-linebacker-barkevious-mingo |archive-date=March 18, 2018 |access-date=March 18, 2018 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Mingo competed against [[D. J. Alexander]] to be a starting outside linebacker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patton |first=Andy |date=July 25, 2018 |title=Will Seahawks linebacker DJ Alexander step into a bigger role? |url=https://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/2018/07/25/linebacker-dj-alexander-bigger-role/ |access-date=January 3, 2019 |website=Seahawks Wire |publisher=USA Today |archive-date=January 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103210352/https://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/2018/07/25/linebacker-dj-alexander-bigger-role/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Head coach [[Pete Carroll]] named Mingo and [[K. J. Wright]] the starting outside linebackers to begin the regular season. They started alongside middle linebacker [[Bobby Wagner]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Seattle Seahawks Depth Chart: 10/01/2018 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/213/SEA |access-date=January 3, 2019 |website=Ourlads.com |archive-date=December 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181205003813/https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/213/SEA |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 6, Mingo collected a season-high seven solo tackles during a 27–3 victory at the [[2018 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Oakland Raiders – October 14th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201810140rai.htm |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211044324/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201810140rai.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the season with a career-high 48 combined tackles (37 solo), two forced fumbles, a pass deflection, and one sack in 16 games and 14 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Barkevious Mingo 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MingBa00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710190437/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MingBa00/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On August 31, 2019, the Seahawks traded Mingo along with outside linebacker [[Jacob Martin (American football)|Jacob Martin]] and a [[2020 NFL draft|2020]] third-round pick to the [[Houston Texans]] in exchange for [[Jadeveon Clowney]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Seahawks acquire DE Jadeveon Clowney from Texans |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/seahawks-acquire-de-jadeveon-clowney-from-texans-0ap3000001045863 |access-date=August 31, 2019 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=August 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831194409/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001045863/article/seahawks-acquire-de-jadeveon-clowney-from-texans |url-status=live }}</ref> In the 2019 season, Mingo mainly had a special teams role but had one start on defense, against the [[2019 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New England Patriots at Houston Texans – December 1st, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201912010htx.htm |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=September 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210907174605/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201912010htx.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Barkevious Mingo 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MingBa00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710184929/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MingBa00/gamelog/2019/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On April 3, 2020, the [[Chicago Bears]] signed Mingo to a one-year, $1.187 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=March 23, 2020 |title=Barkevious Mingo agrees to one-year deal with Bears |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/22/barkevious-mingo-agrees-to-one-year-deal-with-bears/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605201030/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/22/barkevious-mingo-agrees-to-one-year-deal-with-bears/ |archive-date=June 5, 2023 |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=April 3, 2020 |title=Roster Moves: Bears sign OLBs Mingo, Irving |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-mingo-irving |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ChicagoBears.com |archive-date=April 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200406035212/https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-mingo-irving |url-status=live }}</ref>  In a week 9 loss to the [[2020 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]], Mingo was credited with the first rushing attempt of his career, gaining 11 yards and a first down after taking a hand-off on a fake punt.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Tennessee Titans – November 8th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011080oti.htm |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |archive-date=November 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201115121836/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011080oti.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He appeared in 16 games and started three in the 2020 season. He finished with 2.5 sacks, 35 total tackles, and two passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Barkevious Mingo 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MingBa00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710184930/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MingBa00/gamelog/2020/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On March 25, 2021, Mingo signed a one-year contract with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Deighton |first=John |date=March 25, 2021 |title=Falcons Sign RB Mike Davis, LB Barkevious Mingo and CB Fabian Moreau |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/report-falcons-to-sign-running-back-mike-davis |access-date=March 25, 2021 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |archive-date=March 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210324162745/https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/report-falcons-to-sign-running-back-mike-davis |url-status=live }}</ref> His contract was terminated on July 10, following his arrest.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2021 |title=Falcons release LB Mingo after indecency charge |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31795509/atlanta-falcons-barkevious-mingo-arrested-charge-indecency-child |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |archive-date=January 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129001054/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31795509/atlanta-falcons-barkevious-mingo-arrested-charge-indecency-child |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mingo is the son of Hugh Mingo and Barbara Johnson. His unusual first name was created by his mother, adding the first three letters of her first name to a name she liked, Kevious.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lawrence |first=Andrew |date=April 15, 2013 |title=And Mingo Was His Name |url=https://vault.si.com/vault/2013/04/15/and-mingo-was-his-name |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated Vault |language=en-us |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710183255/https://vault.si.com/vault/2013/04/15/and-mingo-was-his-name |url-status=live }}</ref> He has two brothers, Hugh and Hughtavious, who have a similar naming convention after their father.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Nathan|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/5-things-you-may-not-know-about-barkevious-mingo|title=5 things you may not know about Barkevious Mingo|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=September 10, 2025}}</ref>

On July 7, 2021, Mingo was arrested in [[Arlington, Texas|Arlington]], [[Texas]], on a second-degree felony charge of indecency and sexual contact with a minor. He was later released the following day on $25,000 bond.<ref name="espn">{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2021 |title=Atlanta Falcons' Barkevious Mingo Arrested on Charge of Indecency with Child |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31795509/atlanta-falcons-barkevious-mingo-arrested-charge-indecency-child |access-date=July 10, 2021 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=July 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210710191105/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31795509/atlanta-falcons-barkevious-mingo-arrested-charge-indecency-child |url-status=live }}</ref> The arrest was related to an incident alleged to have occurred in July 2019 involving the teenage friend of a family member.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Wertheim |first=Jon |date=July 10, 2021 |title=Details of the Barkevious Mingo Child Sex Offense Allegation |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2021/07/10/more-details-barkevious-mingo-child-sex-offense-allegations |access-date=October 22, 2021 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us |archive-date=October 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022174541/https://www.si.com/nfl/2021/07/10/more-details-barkevious-mingo-child-sex-offense-allegations |url-status=live }}</ref> The charges were dismissed on December 17, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |date=December 18, 2021 |title=Case against veteran free-agent linebacker Barkevious Mingo dismissed |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32892590/case-veteran-free-agent-linebacker-barkevious-mingo-dismissed |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=June 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605040709/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32892590/case-veteran-free-agent-linebacker-barkevious-mingo-dismissed |url-status=live }}</ref>

starting QB: 3 things to know |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/eye-on-college-football/25279136/reports-baker-mayfield-to-be-named-oklahoma-starting-quarterback |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222230101/https://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/eye-on-college-football/25279136/reports-baker-mayfield-to-be-named-oklahoma-starting-quarterback |archive-date=February 22, 2016 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> He was selected [[List of first overall National Football League Draft picks|first overall]] by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the [[2018 NFL draft]].

Mayfield set the NFL rookie quarterback record for passing touchdowns during his first year, along with ending a 19-game winless streak for the Browns in his debut. His most successful season with the team was in 2020 when he led the Browns to their first playoff appearance since 2002 and first playoff victory since 1994. Following a performance decline and conflict with Browns management, Mayfield was traded from Cleveland for a third round pick in 2022, spending the year with the [[Carolina Panthers]] and [[Los Angeles Rams]].

In 2023, Mayfield joined the Buccaneers, leading the team to two consecutive division titles and a playoff victory. He also earned two consecutive [[Pro Bowl]] selections. Mayfield is currently the all-time leader in [[List of NFL career passer rating leaders#Postseason|playoff passer rating]].

==Early life==
Baker Reagan Mayfield was born on April 14, 1995, in [[Austin, Texas]], to James and Gina Mayfield as the younger of two sons.<ref name="TTU" /><ref name=":8" /> James, a [[private equity]] consultant, encountered financial difficulties during his younger son's senior year in high school. These struggles forced the Mayfields to sell their home and live in rental homes.<ref name=":8" /> Mayfield was given his distinctive name, Baker, which was his mother's idea, under the condition by his father that he also be named after the 40th U.S. President [[Ronald Reagan]], which became his middle name.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Dickey |first=Jack |date=November 28, 2017 |title=Welcome to The Baker Mayfield Show |url=https://www.si.com/college/2017/11/28/oklahoma-sooners-baker-mayfield-heisman-playoff |access-date=February 18, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref>

Mayfield grew up as a fan of the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|University of Oklahoma]]; he attended a number of their games during his childhood.<ref name=":7" /> His father played football for three years at the [[Houston Cougars football|University of Houston]], though he never [[Varsity letter|lettered]].<ref name=":8" />

Mayfield was the starting quarterback for the [[Lake Travis High School]] Cavaliers [[high school football|football team]] in Austin.<ref name=":9">{{Cite news |date= September 25, 2018 |title=A look back at Baker Mayfield's career, from Lake Travis to Norman |language=en |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/news/2017/12/09/a-look-back-at-baker-mayfields-career-from-lake-travis-to-norman/10128435007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190106231458/https://www.statesman.com/news/20171209/a-look-back-at-baker-mayfields-career-from-lake-travis-to-norman |archive-date=January 6, 2019}}</ref> He led Lake Travis to a 25–2 record in two seasons and won the 2011 4A State Championship.<ref name=":9" /> He finished his high school football career totaling 6,255 passing yards, 67 [[touchdown]]s, and eight [[Interceptions#American/Canadian football|interceptions]].<ref name="TTU" /> He was offered scholarships by [[Washington State University|Washington State]], [[Rice University|Rice]], [[New Mexico Lobos football|New Mexico]] and [[Florida Atlantic University|Florida Atlantic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zimmerlee |first=Connor |date=August 10, 2022 |title=Former Red Raider QB Baker Mayfield Among Best Walk-Ons in College Football History |url=https://www.si.com/college/texas-tech/football/red-raiders-quarterback-baker-mayfield-best-walk-ons-college-football-history-ncaa |access-date=December 4, 2024 |website=Texas Tech Red Raiders On SI |language=en-US}}</ref> Mayfield said "I easily could've gone to a place like Florida Atlantic, but my dad pushed me to realize that my dream was to play somewhere big." He chose to go to [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech]], where he was a walk-on.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nkukmbu |first=Nate |date=October 31, 2017 |title=Oklahoma's Heisman hopeful Baker Mayfield could have played for the Owls |url=https://www.upressonline.com/2017/10/oklahomas-heisman-hopeful-baker-mayfield-could-have-played-for-the-owls/ |access-date=February 18, 2024 |website=UP Press – Florida Atlantic}}</ref>

==College career==

===Texas Tech===
====2013 season====
Shortly before the start of the [[2013 Texas Tech Red Raiders football team|2013 season]], Mayfield was named as the starting quarterback following a back injury to projected starter and former [[Lake Travis High School|Lake Travis]] quarterback [[Michael Brewer]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=[[Jake Trotter|Trotter, Jake]] |date=August 30, 2013 |title=Source: Tech to start Baker Mayfield |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/9614528/texas-tech-red-raiders-start-baker-mayfield-qb-source-says |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107021332/http://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/9614528/texas-tech-red-raiders-start-baker-mayfield-qb-source-says |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> Mayfield was the first [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] [[true freshman]] quarterback to start an [[Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]] season opener at the quarterback position.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Keown |first=Tim |date=August 15, 2016 |title=All He Needs Is Hate |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/id/17284078/oklahoma-sooners-qb-baker-mayfield-used-defying-critics |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107021402/http://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/id/17284078/oklahoma-sooners-qb-baker-mayfield-used-defying-critics |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref>

In his first start against [[2013 SMU Mustangs football team|SMU]], Mayfield passed for 413 yards and four touchdowns. His 43 completions of 60 attempts broke a school record held by [[Billy Joe Tolliver]], and fell only four completions short of the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|NCAA Division I FBS]] single-game record for completions by a freshman, held by [[Luke McCown]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dodd |first=Dennis |date=August 31, 2013 |title=Kingsbury the kingmaker finds another one in head coaching debut |work=[[CBS Sports]] |url=https://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/writer/dennis-dodd/23404211/kingsbury-the-kingmaker-finds-another-one-in-head-coaching-debut |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 4, 2016}}</ref><ref name="FBS_p2">{{Cite web |title=2011 Football Bowl Subdivision Records |url=http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2011/FBS.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107022041/http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2011/FBS.pdf |archive-date=January 7, 2019 |publisher=[[NCAA Football]] |page=2}}</ref> For his performance, Mayfield was named [[Big 12 Conference]] Offensive Player of the Week – the first freshman Texas Tech quarterback to be named so since former Red Raider head coach [[Kliff Kingsbury]] in [[1999 Texas Tech Red Raiders football team|1999]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stevenson |first=Stefan |date=September 2, 2013 |title=Mayfield earns Big 12 honor, a first for Texas Tech since Kingsbury in '99 |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |url=http://www.star-telegram.com/2013/09/02/5127169/walsh-will-start-for-oklahoma.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107022159/https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/article3835868.html |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> The game featured the last four former Lake Travis quarterbacks combined on both teams: [[Garrett Gilbert]], Michael Brewer, Collin Lagasse, and Mayfield.<ref>{{Cite news |last=[[Nick Bromberg|Bromberg, Nick]] |date=August 30, 2013 |title=Texas Tech-SMU matchup features the last four Lake Travis High School quarterbacks |work=[[Yahoo Sports]] |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaaf-dr-saturday/texas-tech-smu-matchup-features-last-four-lake-172617499--ncaaf.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107022323/https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaaf-dr-saturday/texas-tech-smu-matchup-features-last-four-lake-172617499--ncaaf.html |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref>

Following the Red Raiders' second victory over [[2013 Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks football team|Stephen F. Austin]], Mayfield's 780 season yards and seven touchdowns already exceeded the 755 yards and six touchdowns accrued by Texas Tech's last true freshman quarterback, Aaron Keesee, in 10 games.<ref name="Sports Reference 84">{{Cite web |title=1984 Year Summary |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/1984.html |access-date=September 11, 2013 |website=College Football at [[Sports-Reference.com]] |archive-date=April 20, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420190059/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/1984.html |url-status=live }}</ref> After being affected by a knee injury and losing the starting job to fellow true freshman [[Davis Webb]], Mayfield finished the season with 2,315 yards on 218-of-340 completions with 12 touchdowns and 9 interceptions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stavenhagen |first=Cody |date=December 9, 2017 |title=OU football: The weird and wild timeline of Baker Mayfield's journey to the Heisman Trophy |language=en |work=[[Tulsa World]] |url=https://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/ousportsextra/ou-football-the-weird-and-wild-timeline-of-baker-mayfield/article_07dbfcd6-c8da-5ad0-bf06-241d5007636f.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103081857/http://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/ousportsextra/ou-football-the-weird-and-wild-timeline-of-baker-mayfield/article_07dbfcd6-c8da-5ad0-bf06-241d5007636f.html |archive-date=January 3, 2018}}</ref>

Mayfield was named one of 10 semifinalists for the [[Burlsworth Trophy]] in November; the award is given to the best player in Division I football who began his college career as a walk-on.<ref name="Burlsworth">{{Cite news |date=November 19, 2013 |title=Mayfield named semifinalist for the Burlsworth Trophy |work=[[KCBD]] |url=http://www.kcbd.com/story/24014356/mayfield-named-semifinalist-for-the-burlsworth-trophy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107022609/http://www.kcbd.com/story/24014356/mayfield-named-semifinalist-for-the-burlsworth-trophy/ |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref>

Mayfield earned Big 12 Conference Freshman Offensive Player of the Year for the 2013 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Christopher |date=January 24, 2017 |title=Can Baker Mayfield Cap His Career with a Heisman Trophy and 2nd Playoff Berth? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2688746-can-baker-mayfield-cap-his-career-with-a-heisman-trophy-and-2nd-playoff-berth |access-date=February 21, 2019 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en |archive-date=February 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190222041947/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2688746-can-baker-mayfield-cap-his-career-with-a-heisman-trophy-and-2nd-playoff-berth |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="POY">{{Cite news |last=Aber |first=Ryan |date=December 11, 2013 |title=Big 12 football: OU, OSU place combined eight players on All-Big 12 football team |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |url=http://newsok.com/big-12-football-ou-osu-place-combined-eight-players-on-all-big-12-football-team/article/3913522 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107022732/https://newsok.com/article/3913522/big-12-football-ou-osu-place-combined-eight-players-on-all-big-12-football-team |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> Mayfield announced that he would be leaving the program due to a "miscommunication" with the coaching staff.<ref name="transfer">{{Cite news |last=Graham |first=Mike |date=December 11, 2013 |title=Is QB Baker Mayfield seeking a transfer from Texas Tech?
