===Oklahoma===
====2014 season====
After playing for Texas Tech, Mayfield transferred to the [[University of Oklahoma]] in January 2014, but had not contacted the Sooners coaching staff. Mayfield further elaborated in an interview with [[ESPN]] that he sought to transfer due to scholarship issues and a perception that he had earned the starting position and that further competition was not "really fair".<ref name=":1" /><ref name="transfer" /> The alleged scholarship issues were denied by Texas Tech coach Kliff Kingsbury.<ref name="NewsOK">{{Cite news |last=Kersey |first=Jason |date=October 19, 2015 |title=Oklahoma football: How people in Lubbock view Baker Mayfield |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |url=http://newsok.com/article/5454584 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107022956/https://newsok.com/article/5454584/oklahoma-football-how-people-in-lubbock-view-baker-mayfield |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref>

In February 2014, Oklahoma head coach [[Bob Stoops]] confirmed that Mayfield would be walking on for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]]. Mayfield was not eligible to play until the 2015 season, and he lost a season of eligibility due to Big 12 Conference transfer rules following an unsuccessful appeal of his transfer restrictions.<ref name="OU">{{Cite news |last=Shadid |first=Trent |date=February 5, 2014 |title=Bob Stoops confirms Baker Mayfield's transfer from Texas Tech |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |url=http://newsok.com/bob-stoops-confirms-baker-mayfields-transfer-from-texas-tech/article/3930877 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107023054/https://newsok.com/article/3930877/bob-stoops-confirms-baker-mayfields-transfer-from-texas-tech |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref>

====2015 season====
On August 24, 2015, Mayfield was named the starting quarterback for the [[2015 Oklahoma Sooners football team|Sooners]] after winning an open quarterback competition against [[Trevor Knight]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 24, 2015 |title=Oklahoma names Mayfield as starting QB over incumbent Knight |work=[[Fox Sports]] |url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-football/story/oklahoma-sooners-baker-mayfield-starting-qb-over-trevor-knight-082415 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190530142433/https://www.foxsports.com/college-football/story/oklahoma-sooners-baker-mayfield-starting-qb-over-trevor-knight-082415 |archive-date=May 30, 2019}}</ref> On September 6, 2015, Mayfield started against [[2015 Akron Zips football team|Akron]]. Mayfield totaled 388 passing yards with three passing touchdowns on 23 completions in the 41–3 win.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 6, 2015 |title=Mayfield leads No. 19 Oklahoma past Akron 41–3 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=400763404 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107023234/http://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=400763404 |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> In the second game of the 2015 season, Mayfield started at [[2015 Tennessee Volunteers football team|Tennessee]] at [[Neyland Stadium]]. The Sooners were ranked 19th at the time and the Volunteers were ranked 23rd. Mayfield started off very slow in the game, not even reaching midfield until the 13-minute mark of the fourth quarter. Oklahoma came back from a 17-point deficit to win the game by a score of 31–24 in double overtime. Mayfield threw for 187 yards and three touchdowns on 19 completions while throwing two interceptions early in the game.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Sooners surge from 17 points down to edge Tennessee in double overtime |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=400603868 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107023342/http://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=400603868 |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> In the third game of the season, Mayfield started against [[2015 Tulsa Golden Hurricane football team|Tulsa]]. He had a career day, throwing for 487 yards and four touchdowns, including 316 yards in the first half. Mayfield also ran for 85 yards and two touchdowns in the 52–38 win.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 19, 2015 |title=Mayfield sets record for total yards as No. 16 Oklahoma beats Tulsa |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=400763418 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107023713/http://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=400763418 |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bailey |first=Eric |date=September 20, 2015 |title=Air Apparent: Baker Mayfield needs record-setting day for OU to beat Tulsa |work=[[Tulsa World]] |url=https://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/ousportsextra/no-oklahoma-vs-tulsa-baker-mayfield-s-big-half-has/article_a819258c-fd31-5c3d-9647-47d83a0c4e4b.html |access-date=January 7, 2019 |archive-date=September 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925001302/https://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/ousportsextra/no-oklahoma-vs-tulsa-baker-mayfield-s-big-half-has/article_a819258c-fd31-5c3d-9647-47d83a0c4e4b.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Mayfield finished the year with 3,700 passing yards, 36 touchdowns, and seven interceptions, a résumé which propelled him to fourth place in voting for the [[Heisman Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Trahan |first=Kevin |date=December 13, 2015 |title=Full Heisman Trophy 2015 voting results: The Stanford runner-up tradition continues |work=[[SB Nation]] |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2015/12/12/10015764/2015-heisman-trophy-voting-results-ballots |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190530142819/https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2015/12/12/10015764/2015-heisman-trophy-voting-results-ballots |archive-date=May 30, 2019}}</ref> Mayfield helped lead Oklahoma to the [[2015 Orange Bowl]], which served as the semifinal for the 2015 [[College Football Playoff]]. However, Oklahoma lost to [[2015 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson]] by a score of 37–17.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Orange Bowl – Oklahoma vs Clemson Box Score, December 31, 2015 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2015-12-31-clemson.html |access-date=September 10, 2017 |website=College Football at [[Sports-Reference.com]] |archive-date=April 20, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420102117/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2015-12-31-clemson.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2016 season====
Mayfield started off the 2016 season with 323 passing yards and two touchdowns in a 33–23 loss to #15 [[2016 Houston Cougars football team|Houston]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 5, 2016 |title=Oklahoma QB Mayfield takes blame for loss to Houston |language=en |work=[[USA Today]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2016/09/05/oklahoma-qb-mayfield-takes-blame-for-loss-to-houston/89889632/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107024037/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2016/09/05/oklahoma-qb-mayfield-takes-blame-for-loss-to-houston/89889632/ |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> In the rivalry game against [[2016 Texas Longhorns football|Texas]] on October 8, he had 390 passing yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the 45–40 victory.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gosset |first=Brian |date=October 8, 2016 |title=Charlie Strong's case no better after Texas falls to No. 20 Oklahoma |language=en |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-texas/article106998882.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107024154/https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-texas/article106998882.html |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> On October 22, in a [[2016 Oklahoma vs. Texas Tech football game|66–59 victory]] over [[2016 Texas Tech Red Raiders football team|Texas Tech]], Mayfield had 545 passing yards and seven touchdowns in a historic matchup against future NFL quarterback [[Patrick Mahomes]]. Mahomes tallied 734 passing yards and five touchdowns to go along with Mayfield's numbers in a game that broke various single-game passing records.<ref>{{Cite news |last=[[Jake Trotter|Trotter, Jake]] |date=October 23, 2016 |title=Baker Mayfield outduels record-setting Patrick Mahomes II in return to Lubbock |language=en |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/big12/post/_/id/115714/mayfield-outduels-record-setting-mahomes-in-return-to-lubbock |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107024252/http://www.espn.com/blog/big12/post/_/id/115714/mayfield-outduels-record-setting-mahomes-in-return-to-lubbock |archive-date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> Over the final five games of the regular season, Mayfield totaled 1,321 passing yards, 15 passing touchdowns, and three interceptions, to go along with three rushing touchdowns. All five games were victories for the Sooners.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baker Mayfield 2016 Game Log (Games 8–12) |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/baker-mayfield-1/gamelog/2016/#29-33-sum:gamelog |access-date=October 29, 2018 |website=College Football at [[Sports-Reference.com]] |language=en |archive-date=February 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207065907/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/baker-mayfield-1/gamelog/2016#29-33-sum:gamelog |url-status=live }}</ref>

In December 2016, it was announced that Mayfield and his top receiving target, [[Dede Westbrook]], would be finalists for the 2016 [[Heisman Trophy]]. It was also announced that they would play in the [[2017 Sugar Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guillory |first=William |date=January 2, 2017 |title=Oklahoma's Baker Mayfield, Dede Westbrook look for Sugar Bowl win to complete 'phenomenal' season |url=https://www.nola.com/sugarbowl/2017/01/oklahomas_baker_mayfield_dede.html |access-date=February 21, 2019 |website=nola.com |language=en-US |archive-date=February 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190222042121/https://www.nola.com/sugarbowl/2017/01/oklahomas_baker_mayfield_dede.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Mayfield ended up finishing third in the Heisman voting.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Heisman Trophy Voting |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/awards/heisman-2016.html |access-date=September 10, 2017 |website=College Football at [[Sports-Reference.com]] |archive-date=April 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419235642/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/awards/heisman-2016.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the 2017 Sugar Bowl, Mayfield helped lead the Sooners to a 35–19 victory over [[2016 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]]. He finished the game with 19 completions on 28 attempts for 296 passing yards and two touchdowns, earning him the MVP award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sugar Bowl – Auburn vs Oklahoma Box Score, January 2, 2017 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2017-01-02-oklahoma.html |access-date=September 10, 2017 |website=College Football at [[Sports-Reference.com]] |archive-date=April 20, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420132412/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2017-01-02-oklahoma.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==="Baker Mayfield rule"===
When Mayfield transferred from Texas Tech to Oklahoma after his freshman year, he filed an appeal to the [[NCAA]] to allow him to be eligible to play immediately at Oklahoma on the basis that he was a walk-on and not a scholarship player at Texas Tech; therefore, the transfer rules that apply to scholarship players should not be applicable to his situation. The NCAA denied his appeal because he did not meet the criteria. [[Big 12 Conference]] rules additionally stipulated that intra-conference transfers will lose one year of eligibility over and beyond the one-year sit-out imposed by the NCAA.<ref name="Rule4">{{Cite web |title=Conference Handbook |url=http://www.big12sports.com/fls/10410/pdfs/handbook/ConferenceHandbook.pdf |access-date=September 3, 2016 |website=Big12Sports.com |publisher=Big 12 Conference |archive-date=September 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190905200716/http://www.big12sports.com/fls/10410/pdfs/handbook/ConferenceHandbook.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> Mayfield attempted to appeal his initial loss of eligibility to the Big 12 Conference faculty athletics representatives but was denied in September 2014.<ref name="rule3">{{Cite web |last=Aber |first=Ryan |date=December 17, 2015 |title=OU football journal: Baker Mayfield named The Sporting News' Player of the Year |url=http://newsok.com/article/5467486 |access-date=September 3, 2016 |publisher=NewsOK |archive-date=May 3, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170503173926/http://newsok.com/article/5467486 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Officials from Oklahoma asked Texas Tech officials to authorize Mayfield's immediate eligibility, but Texas Tech officials objected and declined the request before granting a release in July 2014.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fowler |first=Jeremy |date=August 21, 2014 |title=Texas Tech lifts scholarship ban for OU's Baker Mayfield |work=[[CBS Sports]] |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/texas-tech-lifts-scholarship-ban-for-ous-baker-mayfield/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190110032444/https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/texas-tech-lifts-scholarship-ban-for-ous-baker-mayfield/ |archive-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref> Mayfield was thus forced to sit out the [[2014 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2014 season]], while also losing one year of eligibility, as required by the rules.<ref>{{Cite news |last=[[Jake Trotter|Trotter, Jake]] |date=September 29, 2014 |title=Baker Mayfield has appeal denied |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/11612827/oklahoma-baker-mayfield-appeal-denied-ncaa |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190110032510/http://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/11612827/oklahoma-baker-mayfield-appeal-denied-ncaa |archive-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Tramel |first=Berry |date=January 31, 2016 |title=Could Baker Mayfield transfer and get his fourth season elsewhere? |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |url=https://newsok.com/article/5475949/could-baker-mayfield-transfer-and-get-his-fourth-season-elsewhere |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190110032607/https://newsok.com/article/5475949/could-baker-mayfield-transfer-and-get-his-fourth-season-elsewhere |archive-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref>

On June 1, 2016, the Big 12 faculty athletic representatives voted against a rule proposal that would have allowed walk-on players to transfer within the conference and not lose a year of eligibility. The next day, the rule proposal was amended to allow walk-on players, without a written scholarship offer from the school they are transferring from, to transfer within the conference without losing a season of eligibility. The faculty athletic representatives approved the amended proposal with a vote of 7–3. The rule change made Mayfield eligible to play for Oklahoma through the 2017 season. Texas Tech voted in favor of the rule.<ref>{{Cite news |last=[[Jake Trotter|Trotter, Jake]] |date=June 2, 2016 |title=Baker Mayfield eligible for OU in '17 after Big 12 OK's tweaked rule |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/15912568/big-12-reversal-makes-baker-mayfield-eligible-oklahoma-sooners-2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190110032734/http://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/15912568/big-12-reversal-makes-baker-mayfield-eligible-oklahoma-sooners-2017 |archive-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hoover |first=John |date=July 18, 2016 |title=Kingsbury: Texas Tech voted for 'Baker Mayfield Rule' |work=[[KRXO-FM]] |url=http://thefranchiseok.com/kingsbury-texas-tech-voted-for-baker-mayfield-rule/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170410074031/http://thefranchiseok.com/kingsbury-texas-tech-voted-for-baker-mayfield-rule/ |archive-date=April 10, 2017}}</ref>

While the injury was not severe, coach [[Kevin Stefanski]] decided not to put him in for the rest of the game due to Mayfield absorbing hits and the game being out of reach.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Nate |date=November 14, 2021 |title=Browns QB Baker Mayfield leaves game with knee injury |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/browns/2021/11/14/baker-mayfield-injury-cleveland-browns-quarterback/8617917002/ |access-date=November 15, 2021 |website=USA Today |language=en |archive-date=November 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211114220748/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/browns/2021/11/14/baker-mayfield-injury-cleveland-browns-quarterback/8617917002/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After the Browns were eliminated from the postseason following a Week 17 loss to the Steelers, the Browns announced Mayfield would undergo surgery on the torn labrum, ending Mayfield's season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=January 4, 2022 |title=Baker Mayfield ruled out for Week 18; ===Los Angeles Rams===
{{see also|2022 Los Angeles Rams season}}
On December 6, 2022, Mayfield was claimed off waivers by the Rams after starting quarterback [[Matthew Stafford]] sustained a spinal cord injury on December 2.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=December 6, 2022 |title=Rams claimed and awarded QB Baker Mayfield off waivers |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-claimed-and-awarded-qb-baker-mayfield-off-waivers |access-date=December 6, 2022 |website=therams.com |archive-date=December 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206212648/https://www.therams.com/news/rams-claimed-and-awarded-qb-baker-mayfield-off-waivers |url-status=live }}</ref> The Rams inherited the remaining $1.35 million on his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinnan |first=Cory |date=December 6, 2022 |title=Baker Mayfield claimed by Rams after requesting release from Panthers |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/baker-mayfield-claimed-rams-requesting-213843976.html |access-date=December 10, 2022 |website=Yahoo! Entertainment |archive-date=December 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221210235604/https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/baker-mayfield-claimed-rams-requesting-213843976.html |url-status=live }}</ref> With only two days for Mayfield to learn the playbook after he was claimed, the Rams started [[John Wolford]] at quarterback for their game against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]]. Rams' head coach [[Sean McVay]] benched Wolford after the first offensive series, though, and inserted Mayfield. The Rams were trailing 16–3 in the fourth quarter, seemingly headed for their seventh consecutive loss, when Mayfield led them on a comeback. With 1:45 remaining in the game, still down by 6 points, and with no timeouts left to use, the Rams' offense took the field at their own two-yard line. Mayfield then led the Rams to a game-winning 98-yard drive, which became the longest touchdown drive of his career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=December 9, 2022 |title=Mayfield caps Rams debut with 98-yard GW drive |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35213186/rams-list-baker-mayfield-active-thursday-night-vs-raiders |access-date=October 27, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Breech |first=John |date=December 9, 2022 |title=Raiders stunned by Rams: Here are six shocking facts from Baker Mayfield's improbable comeback win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/raiders-stunned-by-rams-here-are-six-shocking-facts-from-baker-mayfields-improbable-comeback-win/ |access-date=December 10, 2022 |work=CBS Sports |archive-date=December 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221210044938/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/raiders-stunned-by-rams-here-are-six-shocking-facts-from-baker-mayfields-improbable-comeback-win/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Mayfield completed 22 of 35 passes for 230 yards without an interception in the game and was named the [[National Football Conference]] Offensive Player of the Week.<ref name="Gordon">{{cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2022-week-14-trevor-lawrence-baker-mayfield |title=Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence, Rams QB Baker Mayfield highlight Players of the Week |work=NFL.com |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=December 14, 2022 |access-date=December 30, 2022 |archive-date=December 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221228172534/https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2022-week-14-trevor-lawrence-baker-mayfield |url-status=live }}</ref>

In a Week 15 ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' matchup against the [[Green Bay Packers]], Mayfield threw his 100th career passing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Barshop|first=Sarah|date=December 9, 2022|title=No Baker Mayfield magic as Rams eliminated by Packers|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35288659/no-baker-mayfield-magic-rams-eliminated-packers|access-date=December 19, 2022|website=[[ESPN]]|archive-date=December 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221220052050/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35288659/no-baker-mayfield-magic-rams-eliminated-packers?platform=amp|url-status=live}}</ref> In a Week 16 matchup against the Broncos, Mayfield led the Rams to a dominant 51–14 win while completing 24 of 28 pass attempts for 230 yards and throwing for two touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35319352/rams-blowout-broncos-russell-wilson-struggles |title=Broncos get blown out by Rams; Russell Wilson throws 3 INTs |work=ESPN |last1=Barshop |first1=Sarah |last2=Legwold |first2=Jeff |date=December 25, 2022 |access-date=December 30, 2022 |archive-date=December 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221231023900/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35319352/rams-blowout-broncos-russell-wilson-struggles |url-status=live }}</ref>

Mayfield would later credit his five-game stint with the Rams for rejuvenating his career following the disappointment of his time with Carolina. “It brought the fun back. When I’m having fun, talking trash, and enjoying it, like that’s when I’m my best. Yeah, I needed that,” Mayfield said.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gulflive.com/buccaneers/2024/07/bucs-qb-baker-mayfield-pinpoints-the-exact-turning-point-in-his-career.html |title=Bucs QB Baker Mayfield pinpoints the exact turning point in his career |work=GulfLive |last1=Maura |first1=Carey |date=July 7, 2024 |access-date=September 23, 2024}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
====2023 season====
{{see also|2023 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season}}
On March 15, 2023, the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] signed Mayfield to a one-year, $4.00 million contract that includes a signing bonus of $2.87 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 16, 2023 |title=Jason Licht: Bucs Have Agreed to Terms with QB Baker Mayfield |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/jason-licht-bucs-agreed-terms-qb-baker-mayfield-free-agency-2023 |access-date=August 1, 2023 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> Mayfield was brought in to compete against [[Kyle Trask]] and [[John Wolford]] to determine who would be the successor at starting quarterback to [[Tom Brady]] after he retired after the 2022 NFL season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Laine |first=Jenna |title=How Baker Mayfield won over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' locker room |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/39288021/how-baker-mayfield-won-tampa-bay-buccaneers-locker-room |access-date=December 16, 2024 |work=ESPN |date=January 15, 2024}}</ref>

In Week 1 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Mayfield went 3 for 11 to start the game, but soon thereafter threw a touchdown to end the first half. After that, Mayfield went 18/23 for 110 yards and a touchdown for the rest of the game, including a crucial scramble for a first down to secure a 20–17 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buccaneers 20–17 Vikings (Sep 10, 2023) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/401547398 |access-date=September 26, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 2 against the [[Chicago Bears]], Mayfield went 26 for 34 for 317 yards and one touchdown in a 27–17 win. His 76% completion percentage for this game narrowly marked the best completion rate of his career at that point, in any of 33 games with 33+ pass attempts. Before that, his 75.8% completion rate on December 6, 2020, in a win against the Titans while on the Browns, had been his highest completion rate. This was also the first time in his career that Mayfield had started 2–0.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodall |first=Fred |date=September 17, 2023 |title=Mayfield shines again, Buccaneers stay unbeaten with 27–17 victory over struggling Bears |url=https://apnews.com/article/bears-buccaneers-nfl-mayfield-fields-b66798d94380dafb1c8241fc45e68ce8 |access-date=September 26, 2023 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> In Week 3 against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], Mayfield went 15/25 for 146 yards, with one touchdown and one interception, his first turnover of the season. He had one rush for 2 yards and fumbled once, which was recovered by Tampa Bay. Mayfield was also sacked twice.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2023 |title=Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield: Underwhelming effort in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/buccaneers-baker-mayfield-underwhelming-effort-in-loss/ |access-date=September 26, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 15 against the Packers, Mayfield posted a [[List of NFL quarterbacks who have posted a perfect passer rating|perfect passer rating]], completing 22 of 28 passes for 381 yards and four touchdowns in a 34–20 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buccaneers 34–20 Packers (Dec 17, 2023) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/401547598 |access-date=February 18, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He was the first opposing quarterback to ever have a perfect passer rating at [[Lambeau Field]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Skinner |first=Caleb |date=December 19, 2023 |title=Buccaneers' QB Baker Mayfield Makes NFL History at Lambeau Field Against Packers |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/buccaneers/news/buccaneers-qb-baker-mayfield-makes-nfl-history-at-lambeau-field-against-packers |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=Tampa Bay Buccaneers {{!}} BucsGameday {{!}} Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> He was named the [[National Football Conference]] (NFC) Offensive Player of the Week for this performance.<ref name="nfc-opoy-w15-2023">{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=December 20, 2023 |title=Bills RB James Cook, Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bills-rb-james-cook-buccaneers-qb-baker-mayfield-highlight-players-of-the-week |access-date=January 19, 2024 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 18 against the Panthers, Mayfield led the Buccaneers to a 9–0 victory, clinching the Buccaneers' third straight [[NFC South]] title.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=January 7, 2024 |title=Bucs Make Franchise History with Third Straight NFC South Title |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/buccaneers-win-nfc-south-playoff-berth-2023-vs-panthers |access-date=January 11, 2024 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> Mayfield concluded the season with 28 touchdown passes, 4,044 passing yards and a 64.3% completion rate, all career highs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Siddiqi |first=DJ |date=January 7, 2024 |title=Baker Mayfield Completes Comeback Player Of The Year Bid, Leads Tampa Bay Buccaneers To Division Title |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/djsiddiqi/2024/01/07/baker-mayfield-completes-tampa-bay-buccaneers-surprising-season-leads-team-to-division-title/?sh=1cc3ba587b6b |access-date=January 11, 2024 |website=Forbes.com}}</ref> He earned his first Pro Bowl nomination.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/probowl.htm |access-date=February 18, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 32, Philadelphia Eagles 9|Wild Card Round]] game against the Eagles, Mayfield completed 22 of 36 passes, for 337 yards, with three touchdowns and no interceptions. He led the Buccaneers to a 32–9 win over the defending NFC champions.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Laine |first1=Jenna |last2=McManus |first2=Tim |date=January 16, 2024 |title=Baker Mayfield, Bucs eliminate defending NFC champion Eagles |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/39315507/tampa-bay-buccaneers-eliminate-defending-nfc-champion-philadelphia-eagles |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC: Detroit Lions 31, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2|Divisional round]] against the [[Detroit Lions]], Mayfield completed 26 of 41 passes for 349 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions. The second interception proved costly as it allowed the Lions to run out the clock as the Buccaneers lost, 31–23.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Suggs |first=David |date=January 22, 2024 |title=Lions vs. Buccaneers final score, results: Detroit outlasts Tampa to clinch first NFC Championship appearance since 1991 |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/lions-buccaneers-live-score-highlights-2024-nfl-playoffs/105f55ff71361dccb41e174d |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=Sporting News |language=en-us}}</ref>

====2024 season====
{{see also|2024 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season}}
On March 10, 2024, Mayfield signed a three-year contract extension with the Buccaneers, worth up to $100 million, with $50 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 11, 2024 |title=More Time to Bake! Baker Mayfield Agrees to New Deal with Bucs |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/baker-mayfield-agrees-new-deal-bucs |access-date=March 10, 2024 |website=Tampa Bay Buccaneers}}</ref> In Week 1, Mayfield went 24-of-30 for 289 yards and four touchdowns in a 37–20 win over the Commanders.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 8, 2024 |title=Baker Mayfield throws four TDs in 37-20 Bucs win |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/baker-mayfield-throws-four-tds-232806352.html |access-date=September 9, 2024 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> In a rematch of last season's Divisional round playoff game, Mayfield completed 12 passes for 185 yards and ran for a go-ahead touchdown as the Buccaneers beat the Lions 20–16.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 15, 2024 |title=Mayfield runs for a TD and throws a TD pass, lifting Bucs to 20-16 win over Lions in playoff rematch |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/mayfield-runs-td-throws-td-202636517.html |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Yahoo! Sports|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> After a poor performance against the [[Denver Broncos]], Mayfield rebounded the following week against the Eagles, throwing for 347 yards and accounting for three touchdowns as Tampa improved to 3–1.<ref>{{cite news |last=Goodall |first=Fred |title=Mayfield throws for 347 yards and accounts for three TDs to lead Bucs over Eagles 33-16 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/mayfield-throws-347-yards-accounts-203521209.html |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Yahoo Sports |date=September 29, 2024}}</ref> In Week 5 against the Falcons, Mayfield threw three touchdown passes in the first half, but a lack of efficiency on offense in the second half cost the Buccaneers as they lost in overtime.<ref>{{cite news |title=Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield: Trio of touchdowns in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/buccaneers-baker-mayfield-trio-of-touchdowns-in-loss/ |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=CBS Sports |date=October 4, 2024}}</ref> In Week 6, Mayfield threw for 325 yards, four touchdown passes, and overcame three interceptions in the second quarter to win 51–27 against the Saints, leading the offense to a franchise record 594 yards.<ref>{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Scott |title=Unstoppable Bucs Pull Away in Second Half for 51-27 Win in New Orleans |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-saints-week-6-recap-postgame-report |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Buccaneers.com |date=October 13, 2024}}</ref>

In a 41–31 loss to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in Week 7, Mayfield threw for 370 yards and three touchdowns, but he threw a pair of costly interceptions in the first half and lost receivers [[Mike Evans (wide receiver)|Mike Evans]] and [[Chris Godwin]], the latter of whom ruled out for the season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Goodall |first=Fred |title=Injuries to WRs Godwin and Evans will test Tampa Bay's depth and resiliency |url=https://apnews.com/article/buccaneers-analysis-week-7-374759e3b78f408434a64957606f2e1d |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Associated Press |date=October 22, 2024}}</ref> Without his top receivers, Mayfield still completed a career-high 37 passes the following week against the Falcons.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bucs' Offense Dominating on Third Down |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-offense-dominating-third-down-data-crunch |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Buccaneers.com |date=October 28, 2024}}</ref> He finished with over 300 yards and three touchdowns for the third straight game but threw two interceptions inside the Falcons' 10-yard line as the Buccaneers lost 31–26.<ref>{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Scott |title=Turnovers Stop Bucs From Keeping Pace in Shootout Loss to Falcons |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-falcons-week-8-recap-postgame-report |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Buccaneers.com |date=October 27, 2024}}</ref> Mayfield cut down on his interception miscues and led last-minute game-tying drives against the Chiefs and 49ers, but the Buccaneers lost both games, dropping to 4–6 heading to their bye week.<ref>{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Scott |title=49ers Walk It Off, Sending Bucs to Fourth Straight Loss |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-49ers-week-10-recap-postgame-report |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Buccaneers.com |date=November 11, 2024}}</ref> With the return of Mike Evans following the bye, Mayfield had an efficient game against the Giants, completing 24 of 30 passes for 294 yards, no interceptions, and a rushing touchdown as the Bucs won 30–7, snapping their four-game skid.<ref>{{cite news |last=Dix |first=Brianna |title=Takeaways from Buccaneers-Giants |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/takeaways-from-buccaneers-giants-week-12-2024 |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Buccaneers.com |date=November 25, 2024}}</ref> Against the Panthers in Week 13, Mayfield rallied from an Achilles injury and a poor first half to lead Tampa to a game-winning field goal drive in overtime.<ref>{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Scott |title=Bucs Rally for Overtime Win Over Panthers, Grab Share of First Place |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-panthers-week-13-recap-postgame-report |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=Buccaneers.com |date=December 2, 2024}}</ref>

Mayfield's play continued to improve with three touchdowns in a win over the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], followed by a near-flawless performance against the league's top-ranked [[Los Angeles Chargers]] defense, completing 22-of-27 passes for 288 yards and four touchdowns in a 40–17 victory.<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 15, 2024 |title=Mayfield throws for 4 TD passes as Buccaneers dominate the second half to rout Chargers 40-17 |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/mayfield-throws-for-4-tds-including-2-to-evans-as-bucs-dominate-second-half-to-rout-chargers-40-17-3/ |access-date=December 17, 2024 |work=CBS News|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In Week 17, Mayfield was 27-for-32 for 359 yards and a career-high five touchdown passes in a 48–14 win over the Panthers, earning NFC Offensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2024 |title=Bengals QB Joe Burrow, Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2024-week-17-joe-burrow-baker-mayfield |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Needing a win against the Saints to clinch the NFC South, Mayfield led three touchdown drives in the second half and rallied his team from a double-digit deficit to secure their fourth straight division title.<ref>{{cite news |last=Maaddi |first=Rob |title=Buccaneers beat Saints 27-19 to clinch NFC South and wide receiver Mike Evans surpasses 1,000 yards |url=https://apnews.com/article/buccaneers-saints-score-0cd1ec6bef12d1cedc7f45cd9972d5a7 |access-date=January 5, 2025 |work=Associated Press |date=January 5, 2025}}</ref> Mayfield finished the season completing 71.4% of his passes for 4,500 yards and 41 passing touchdowns, becoming the fourth player in NFL history to have at least 4,000 passing yards, 40 passing touchdowns, and at least a 70% completion percentage in a single season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Scott |title=Baker Mayfield Joins Exclusive 4,500-40 Club |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/baker-mayfield-data-crunch-week-18-saints-buccaneers |access-date=January 11, 2025 |work=Buccaneers.com |date=January 6, 2025}}</ref> He also tied with [[Kirk Cousins]] for the most interceptions with 16 and fumbles with 13, both of which led the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Qb Most Interceptions 2024 |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/nfl-qb-most-interceptions-2024 |access-date=2025-05-07 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Qb Most Fumbles 2024 |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/nfl-qb-most-fumbles-2024 |access-date=2025-05-07 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref>

Mayfield helped lead the Buccaneers to a playoff berth. In the NFC [[2024–25 NFL playoffs#NFC: Washington Commanders 23, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 20|Wild Card Round]], Mayfield led two touchdown drives and two drives that ended in a field goal. In that game, Mayfield threw for 185 yards completing 83.3% of his passes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Washington Commanders at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - January 12th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202501120tam.htm |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The Buccaneers' season ended in the Wild Card Round with a 23–20 loss to the Washington Commanders.<ref name="t785">{{cite web | last=Maaddi | first=Rob | title=Jayden Daniels leads Commanders to first playoff win in nearly 7,000 days, 23-20 over the Buccaneers | website=AP News | date=2025-01-13 | url=https://apnews.com/article/commanders-buccaneers-nfl-playoffs-score-dbe21728f66be123a55744a260a3de7e | access-date=2025-01-21}}</ref> He was ranked 50th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2025]].<ref>{{Cite web| last=Dix | first=Brianna | date=August 4, 2025 | title= Baker Mayfield Ranked 50 on the NFL's Top 100 Players of 2025 | work=Buccaneers.com | url= https://www.buccaneers.com/news/baker-mayfield-ranked-50-on-the-nfl-top-100-players-of-2025 | access-date=June 2, 2026}}</ref>

====2025 season====
{{main|2025 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season}}
[[File:Baker-Mayfield-vs-Bills-2 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Mayfield and center [[Graham Barton]] warming up before a game against the [[Buffalo Bills]] in 2025]]Mayfield led the Buccaneers to a 5–1 start despite losing Evans and Godwin to injuries again, throwing for 12 touchdowns to just 1 interception during that span and sparking discussion about his candidacy for the [[NFL MVP Award]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Battista |first=Judy |author-link=Judy Battista |date=2025-10-13 |title=Six biggest surprises of the 2025 NFL season so far: Baker Mayfield leads MVP race; Ravens in free fall |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/six-biggest-surprises-of-the-2025-nfl-season-so-far-baker-mayfield-leads-mvp-race-ravens-in-free-fall |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The Buccaneers then proceeded to lose four of the next five games, namely to the [[Detroit Lions]], [[New England Patriots]], [[Buffalo Bills]], and [[Los Angeles Rams]], with Mayfield suffering an injury to his non-throwing shoulder in the loss to the Rams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=November 24, 2025 |title=Mayfield sprains left shoulder in loss; MRI next |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47080295/bucs-baker-mayfield-exits-vs-rams-left-shoulder-injury |access-date=2025-11-29 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2025 season with 3,693 yards, 26 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions to go with a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baker Mayfield 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MayfBa00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On February 25, 2017, Mayfield was arrested in [[Washington County, Arkansas]] on charges of [[public intoxication]], [[disorderly conduct]], and fleeing and [[resisting arrest]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=[[Jake Trotter|Trotter, Jake]] |date=February 25, 2017 |title=Oklahoma QB Baker Mayfield arrested in Arkansas |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/18764103/oklahoma-sooners-quarterback-baker-mayfield-arrested |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111013005/http://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/18764103/oklahoma-sooners-quarterback-baker-mayfield-arrested |archive-date=January 11, 2019}}</ref> At 2:29 a.m. that Saturday, a police officer was flagged down on an assault and battery report. The person who flagged the officer was yelling at Mayfield. The preliminary police report described Mayfield as unable to walk straight, having slurred speech and food covering the front of his shirt. When he was asked to stay so the police could get a statement, Mayfield began shouting obscenities and "causing a scene". Mayfield was booked at 8:21 a.m. local time on the misdemeanor charges. He had a court date on April 7 for the public intoxication charge, and pleaded not guilty to all charges.<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 27, 2017 |title=Hearing set for OU quarterback Baker Mayfield |work=[[KOCO-TV]] |url=http://www.koco.com/article/hearing-set-for-ou-quarterback-baker-mayfield/8984495 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111013102/https://www.koco.com/article/hearing-set-for-ou-quarterback-baker-mayfield/8984495 |archive-date=January 11, 2019}}</ref> On June 15, 2017, the University of Oklahoma ordered Mayfield to perform 35 hours of community service along with completing an alcohol education program.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goodbread |first=Chase |date=June 15, 2017 |title=Oklahoma disciplines Baker Mayfield for February arrest |work=NFL.com |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/oklahoma-disciplines-baker-mayfield-for-february-arrest-0ap3000000815401 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111013216/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000815401/article/oklahoma-disciplines-baker-mayfield-for-february-arrest |archive-date=January 11, 2019}}</ref>

In July 2019, Mayfield married Emily Wilkinson.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Risdon |first=Jeff |date=July 7, 2019 |title=Baker Mayfield and Emily Wilkinson tie the knot |url=https://brownswire.usatoday.com/2019/07/07/baker-mayfield-and-emily-wilkinson-tie-the-knot/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190707132648/https://brownswire.usatoday.com/2019/07/07/baker-mayfield-and-emily-wilkinson-tie-the-knot/ |archive-date=July 7, 2019 |access-date=July 7, 2019 |website=Browns Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en}}</ref> In December 2023, the pair announced they were expecting their first child, a girl, who was born in April 2024.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/39056194/baker-mayfield-emily-mayfield-pregnancy |title=Bucs' Baker Mayfield misinterpreted wife's pregnancy news |website=[[ESPN]] |first=Jenna |last=Laine |date=December 6, 2023 |access-date=December 26, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231216062912/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/39056194/baker-mayfield-emily-mayfield-pregnancy |archive-date=December 16, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hendricks |first=Jaclyn |date=April 13, 2024 |title=Baker Mayfield, wife Emily welcome baby daughter: 'Everything we prayed for' |url=https://nypost.com/2024/04/13/sports/baker-mayfield-wife-emily-welcome-baby-daughter-kova-jade/ |access-date=September 8, 2024 |website=New York Post}}</ref>

During his tenure with the Browns, Mayfield starred in a continuing series of ads for [[Progressive Insurance]]. The ads showed him living "at home" in [[FirstEnergy Stadium]] with his wife and performing household chores like mowing the lawn and holding a yard sale.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Contes |first=Brandon |date=July 13, 2022 |title=Baker Mayfield says Progressive declined his pitch for a "moving out" edition of his 'At Home' commercials |url=https://awfulannouncing.com/advertising/baker-mayfield-progressive-commercials.html |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=Awful Announcing |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[WWE Performance Center]] |debut = October 18, 2012 }} | module2 = {{Infobox NFL biography | embed = yes | name = Thomas Pestock | image = | number = 68, 69 | position = [[Offensive guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 6 | weight_lbs = 317 | college = [[Northwest Missouri State Bearcats football|Northwest Missouri State]] | undraftedyear = 2009 | pastteams = * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|2009}})* * [[Arizona Cardinals]] ({{NFL Year|2010}}–{{NFL Year|2011}})* | highlights = * First Team All-[[Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association|MIAA]] (2008) | pfr = P/PestTo00 }} }} '''Thomas Pestock''' (born September 13, 1984) is an American [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]], [[Brazilian jiu jitsu]] practitioner, former professional [[American football|football]] player and former [[amateur boxer]]. He is now working for [[Major League Wrestling]] (MLW), where he performs under the [[ring name]] '''Bishop Dyer''' and is one-half of the [[MLW World Tag Team Champions]] with [[Donovan Dijak]] in their first reign, while also making appearances on the [[independent circuit]]. He is best known for his tenure in [[WWE]] from 2012 to 2024, where he performed under the [[ring name]] '''Baron Corbin'''. Pestock was an [[offensive lineman]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] and [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League|NFL]], as well as a two-time [[Golden Gloves]] boxing regional champion. He signed with WWE in 2012 and was assigned to their [[Farm team#Professional wrestling|developmental brand]] [[NXT (WWE brand)|NXT]] under the ring name Baron Corbin, portraying a villainous character nicknamed the "Lone Wolf". He debuted on the main roster at [[WrestleMania 32]], winning the [[André the Giant Memorial Battle Royal]]. In 2017, he won the [[Money in the Bank Briefcase]] and the [[WWE United States Championship]] In 2018, he became "Constable Corbin", an on-screen authority figure of ''[[WWE Raw|Raw]]'' and started a feud with [[Kurt Angle]] which culminated at [[WrestleMania 35]], with Corbin emerging victorious in Angle's retirement match. A few months later, he won the [[King of the Ring (2019)|2019 King of the Ring tournament]], thus changing his name to '''King Corbin''' until 2021, when he lost his crown and adopted the character of a destitute man who had lost everything. Two months later, he adopted the name '''Happy Corbin''' and began portraying a cheerful character who had become extremely wealthy from gambling. From September 2021 to April 2022, Corbin formed an alliance with [[Madcap Moss]]. In October 2022, he began using the Baron Corbin name again and was managed by [[John Bradshaw Layfield|JBL]] until 2023, when he returned to NXT and formed a tag team with [[Bron Breakker]]; they won the NXT Tag Team Championship and the 2024 [[Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic]] together. '''George L. "Bam" Bradley II''' (born June 26, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]].

==High school==
Bradley attended [[Trotwood-Madison High School]] and was a two-time Associated Press All-Ohio Division II honoree.

==College career==
Bradley started in 8 games at Pittsburgh, finished his career with 106 tackles, 17 for loss and 4 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bam_bradley_807998.html |title=Bradley's career at Pittsburgh |access-date=May 1, 2017 |archive-date=December 31, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161231133041/http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bam_bradley_807998.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
Bradley signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an undrafted free agent on May 5, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Officially Sign 16 Undrafted Rookie Free Agents|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Officially-Sign-16-Undrafted-Rookie-Free-Agents/a632b33c-26ed-4b7f-99cf-eedf3d5a756f|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=May 5, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115190512/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Officially-Sign-16-Undrafted-Rookie-Free-Agents/a632b33c-26ed-4b7f-99cf-eedf3d5a756f|archivedate=January 15, 2018}}</ref> Bradley made the Ravens 53-man roster as an undrafted rookie, but his rookie season was cut short due to injury. He suffered a torn ACL in Week 2 against the Browns and was placed on injured reserve on September 19, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign Two Offensive Linemen to 53-Man Roster|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Two-Offensive-Linemen-to-53-Man-Roster/6fe0ab81-3e84-417e-94ba-589bc499d448|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023105658/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Two-Offensive-Linemen-to-53-Man-Roster/6fe0ab81-3e84-417e-94ba-589bc499d448|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 23, 2017|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=September 19, 2017}}</ref>

On August 31, 2018, Bradley was placed on the [[physically unable to perform]] list to start the season while recovering from the torn ACL.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Release 10 Players, Send Four to Injured Reserve|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-release-10-players-send-four-to-injured-reserve|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=August 31, 2018}}</ref>

On March 19, 2019, Bradley was released by the Ravens.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Waive ILB Bam Bradley and CB Jaylen Hill|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-waive-ilb-bam-bradley-and-cb-jaylen-hill|author=Brown, Clifton|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=March 19, 2019}}</ref>

'''Baron Browning''' (born February 19, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] and was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Browning attended [[Kennedale High School]] in [[Kennedale, Texas]]. A five star recruit, he played in the 2017 U.S. Army All American Bowl and was a finalist for the [[Butkus Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |date=September 22, 2016 |title=Five-star LB Baron Browning's Army All-American jersey presentation won't halt focus |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/five-star-lb-baron-brownings-army-all-american-jersey-army-all-american-bowl |access-date=May 28, 2023 |work=USA TODAY High School Sports}}</ref> He committed to [[Ohio State University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Landis |first=Bill |date=December 2, 2016 |title=5-star LB Baron Browning commits to Ohio State |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2016/12/baron_browning_commits_to_ohio.html |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=cleveland.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=VanHaaren |first=Tom |date=December 2, 2016 |title=No. 29 prospect Browning commits to Ohio St. |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recruiting/story/_/id/18183616/baron-browning-chooses-ohio-state-buckeyes |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman at Ohio State in 2017, Browning played in 12 games and had 14 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rabinowitz |first=Bill |date=September 11, 2018 |title=Baron Browning growing into Ohio State's middle linebacker role |url=https://www.buckeyextra.com/sports/20180911/baron-browning-growing-into-ohio-states-middle-linebacker-role |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210117085538/https://www.buckeyextra.com/sports/20180911/baron-browning-growing-into-ohio-states-middle-linebacker-role |archive-date=January 17, 2021 |work=Buckeyextra}}</ref> He started three of 12 games his sophomore year in 2018, recording 24 tackles and one sack. He again played in 12 games his junior year in 2019, finishing with 43 tackles and five sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baird |first=Nathan |date=October 10, 2019 |title=Ohio State football's Baron Browning went from feeling abandoned in Columbus to a blazing young bull |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2019/10/ohio-state-footballs-baron-browning-went-from-feeling-abandoned-in-columbus-to-a-blazing-young-bull.html |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=cleveland.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rowland |first=Kyle |date=October 14, 2019 |title=Browning's rise linked to defense's overall improvement |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ohio-state/2019/10/14/ohio-state-baron-browning-defense-improvement/stories/20191014123 |access-date=May 28, 2023 |work=The Blade}}</ref> Browning returned to Ohio State for his senior year in 2020 and was moved from middle linebacker to outside linebacker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crosher |first=Wyatt |date=January 2, 2020 |title=Baron Browning, Drue Chrisman To Return To Ohio State For Senior Seasons – Buckeye Sports Bulletin |url=https://www.buckeyesports.com/baron-browning-drue-chrisman-to-return-to-ohio-state-for-senior-seasons/ |access-date=May 28, 2023 |work=Buckeye Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Means |first=Stephen |date=May 29, 2020 |title=Baron Browning's position change could make him Ohio State football's most dangerous pass-rusher: Buckeye Take |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2020/05/baron-brownings-position-change-could-make-him-ohio-state-footballs-most-dangerous-pass-rusher-buckeye-take.html |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=cleveland.com}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
Browning was drafted by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the third round, 105th overall, of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=April 30, 2021 |title=Broncos select LB Baron Browning with 105th-overall pick in 2021 NFL Draft |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/baron-browning-nfl-draft-linebacker-ohio-state |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract with Denver on July 22, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zachary |date=July 22, 2021 |title=NFL Draft Pick Signings: 7/22/21 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/07/nfl-draft-pick-signings-7-22-21 |access-date=May 28, 2023 |work=Pro Football Rumors}}</ref>

Browning started his tenure with the Broncos as an inside linebacker but was eventually moved to the outside linebacker group.

Browning was placed on the reserve/[[physically unable to perform|PUP]] list to start the 2023 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Broncos make series of transactions to reduce active roster to league-mandated limit |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-make-series-of-transactions-to-reduce-active-roster-to-league-mandated-l |access-date=2024-10-18 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He was activated on October 21, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=October 21, 2023 |title=Broncos activate OLB Baron Browning from Physically Unable to Perform list, place TE Greg Dulcich on IR |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-olb-baron-browning-from-physically-unable-to-perform-list-place |access-date=2024-10-18 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

On September 21, 2024, Browning was placed on injured reserve after suffering a foot injury in Week 2 against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gabriel |first=Parker |date=2024-09-21 |title=Broncos place OLB Baron Browning on injured reserve after foot injury vs. Steelers |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2024/09/21/baron-browning-injured-reserve-foot-injury/ |access-date=2024-09-21 |work=The Denver Post}}</ref> He was activated on October 17.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos activate OLB Baron Browning, CB Damarri Mathis, T Mike McGlinchey from injured reserve|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-olb-baron-browning-cb-damarri-mathis-t-mike-mcglinchey-from-injured-reserve|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=October 17, 2024}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On November 4, 2024, the Broncos traded Browning to the [[Arizona Cardinals]] for a 2025 sixth-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cardinals Deal For Outside Linebacker Baron Browning|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-deal-for-outside-linebacker-baron-browning|first=Darren|last=Urban|website=AZCardinals.com|date=November 4, 2024|accessdate=November 4, 2024}}</ref>

On March 9, 2025, Browning signed a two-year, $15 million extension with the Cardinals, with a potential additional $4 million in incentives.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-09 |title=Cardinals' Baron Browning: Remaining in AZ |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/cardinals-baron-browning-remaining-in-az/ |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=CBS Sports |language=}}</ref>

'''Bailey Michael Zappe''' ({{IPAc-en|'|z|æ|p|i}}, {{Respell|ZAP|ee}})<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2020 |title=Record-Setting Transfer Quarterback Bailey Zappe Signs With WKU Football |url=https://wkusports.com/news/2020/12/27/record-setting-transfer-quarterback-bailey-zappe-signs-with-wku-football.aspx |access-date=May 1, 2022 |website=Western Kentucky University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> (born April 26, 1999)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bailey Zappe Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/Z/ZappBa00.htm |access-date=October 25, 2022 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played his first three seasons of [[college football]] for the [[Houston Christian Huskies football|Houston Baptist Huskies]] and used his last year of eligibility with the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]], setting the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]] season records for passing yards and passing touchdowns. Zappe was selected in the fourth round of the [[2022 NFL draft]] by the [[New England Patriots]], where he spent his first two seasons alternating as a backup and starter. He joined the Browns as a backup in 2024.

==Early life==
Zappe grew up in [[Victoria, Texas]], and attended [[Victoria East High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Buckley |first=Steve |date=October 6, 2022 |title=Buckley: Bailey Zappe, Patriots quarterback and the pride of Victoria, Texas |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3662380/2022/10/06/bailey-zappe-patriots-hometown/ |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=The Athletic |language=en}}</ref> As a senior, he passed for 3,770 yards and 37 touchdowns, while rushing for 633 yards and scoring 15 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Castillo |first=Rey |date=May 23, 2020 |title=Former East QB thankful for college success at HBU |url=https://www.victoriaadvocate.com/advosports/former-east-qb-thankful-for-college-success-at-hbu/article_47520e28-9bb7-11ea-9786-3bdb25a249f7.html |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[Victoria Advocate]]}}</ref> Zappe was not heavily recruited and committed to play [[college football]] at [[Houston Christian University|Houston Baptist University]], which was his only scholarship offer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeyarajah |first=Shehan |date=September 24, 2020 |title=Houston Baptist's Bailey Zappe is America's most underrated quarterback |url=https://www.texasfootball.com/article/2020/09/23/houston-baptist-s-bailey-zappe-is-america%E2%80%99s-most-underrated-quarterback?ref=article_preview_title |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[Dave Campbell's Texas Football]]}}</ref> Victoria East retired Zappe's No. 4 jersey in 2023.<ref>{{cite news |last=Perez |first=Geno |title=Zappe returns home for special honor |url=https://www.crossroadstoday.com/news/top-stories/zappe-returns-home-for-special-honor/article_1381a56a-9b9e-11ed-a577-d388f993444d.html |access-date=October 22, 2024 |work=crossroadstoday.com |date=January 23, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
===Houston Baptist===
Zappe started nine games in his first year for the [[Houston Baptist Huskies football|Huskies]] at Houston Baptist, passing for 1,548 yards with five touchdowns and 10 interceptions while rushing for two more touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dean |first=Richard |date=August 24, 2018 |title=Bailey Zappe named HBU's starting quarterback |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/college/article/Bailey-Zappe-named-HBU-s-starting-quarterback-13181082.php |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[Houston Chronicle]]}}</ref> As a redshirt sophomore, he completed 357 of 560 passes for 3,811 yards with 35 touchdowns and 15 interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olson |first=Max |date=October 1, 2020 |title=Why Bailey Zappe and Houston Baptist are putting up 2020's wildest passing stats |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2107550/2020/10/01/bailey-zappe-houston-baptist-fcs-fbs-passing-records/ |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Paterik |first=Brice |date=September 9, 2020 |title=5 things Texas Tech fans need to know about Houston Baptist: Prolific QB play leads the Husky offense |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-tech-red-raiders/2020/09/09/5-things-texas-tech-fans-need-to-know-about-houston-baptist-prolific-qb-play-leads-the-husky-offense/ |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> As a redshirt junior, he passed for 1,833 yards and 15 touchdowns against one interception in four games in a shortened season after the [[Southland Conference]] fall football season was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Zappe entered the transfer portal after the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Haley |first=Craig |date=December 14, 2020 |title=Houston Baptist QB Zappe enters NCAA transfer portal |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/houston-baptist-qb-zappe-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal-170538581--ncaaf.html |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

===Western Kentucky===
Zappe committed to transfer to [[Western Kentucky University]], following former Houston Baptist offensive coordinator [[Zach Kittley]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2020 |title=QB Zappe signs with Hilltoppers |url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/qb-zappe-signs-with-hilltoppers/article_b9962205-f83c-5ff9-8b39-ad355b9b66a4.html |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]]}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Yates |first=Dominique |date=February 3, 2021 |title=Western Kentucky football recruiting added transfers to 2021 class |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/football/2021/02/03/western-kentucky-football-recruiting-added-transfers-2021-class/4380145001/ |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[The Courier-Journal]]}}</ref> Zappe's top wide receiver at Houston Baptist, [[Jerreth Sterns]], also transferred to Western Kentucky.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olson |first=Max |date=December 27, 2020 |title=QB Zappe signs with Hilltoppers |url=https://theathletic.com/realtime/vb1vlsBOhF1h/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220195415/https://theathletic.com/realtime/vb1vlsBOhF1h/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 20, 2021 |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref><ref name="auto"/> Zappe was named the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Hilltoppers]]' starting quarterback going into the 2021 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacDonald |first=Jared |date=August 3, 2021 |title=Zappe named Tops' starting QB entering fall |url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/zappe-named-tops-starting-qb-entering-fall/article_a01de542-4ca2-5c7c-bd6b-aaa73d1890cf.html |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]]}}</ref> In his first start for Western Kentucky, he passed for 424 yards and seven touchdowns in a 59–21 win over [[Tennessee-Martin Skyhawks football|Tennessee-Martin]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2021 |title=Zappe's 7 TDs lead Western Kentucky rout of UT Martin, 59-21 |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-college-football-kentucky-c42f669cc577b24af592d53a77599024 |access-date=September 7, 2021 |website=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hale |first=David M. |date=September 4, 2021 |title=The fans, the bands, the drama - Week 1 in college football reminds us of what we missed in 2020 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/page/gamedayfinal090421/the-fans-bands-drama-week-1-college-football-reminds-us-missed-2020 |access-date=September 7, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

During the 2021 regular season, Zappe led the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS) passing for 5,545 yards and throwing for 56 touchdowns. Before the [[2021 Boca Raton Bowl]], he had thrown for nearly 1,100 yards more than the second-ranked FBS quarterback ([[Will Rogers (American football)|Will Rogers]] of [[2021 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|Mississippi State]]), and was within striking distance of the FBS records for passing yardage and touchdowns, set by [[B. J. Symons]] of [[2003 Texas Tech Red Raiders football team|Texas Tech]] in 2003 and [[Joe Burrow]] of [[2019 LSU Tigers football team|LSU]] in 2019, respectively. In the [[2021 Boca Raton Bowl]] against the [[Appalachian State Mountaineers football|Appalachian State Mountaineers]], he broke both records, finishing the season with 5,967 passing yards and 62 touchdowns.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Hass |first=Trevor |date=April 30, 2022 |title=4 things to know about Patriots draft pick Bailey Zappe, a record-setting QB |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/new-england-patriots/2022/04/30/bailey-zappe-patriots-nfl-draft-record-setting-quarterback-things-to-know/ |access-date=May 1, 2022 |website=www.boston.com |language=en-US}}</ref>{{efn|[[Blaine Hawkins]] of [[Central Dutch football|Central]] (IA) holds the NCAA record at 63.<ref name="desmoinesregister.com">{{Cite web |date=December 18, 2021 |title=Central quarterback Blaine Hawkins wins the Gagliardi Trophy as the nation's top Division III player |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/2021/12/18/central-quarterback-blaine-hawkins-wins-gagliardi-trophy/8953840002/ |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US}}</ref>}}

=== New England Patriots ===

==== 2022 ====
The [[New England Patriots]] selected Zappe in the fourth round of the [[2022 NFL draft]] with the 137th overall pick.<ref name=":0" /> He was named the third-string quarterback for the 2022 season behind starter [[Mac Jones]] and second-string backup [[Brian Hoyer]].<ref name="2022DepthChart">{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2022 |title=Breaking down Patriots' first depth chart of the 2022 season |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/patriots-depth-chart-breakdown-cuts-53-man-roster-nfl/ |access-date=August 31, 2022 |website=[[CBS Boston]]}}</ref>

When an injury rendered Jones inactive for Week 4 against the [[Green Bay Packers]], Zappe was promoted to the second option behind Hoyer, but made his NFL debut the same game after Hoyer was injured on his first drive.<ref name="RuleOut">{{Cite web |last=Reiss |first=Mike |date=September 30, 2022 |title=New England Patriots rule out QB Mac Jones; Brian Hoyer gets start vs. Green Bay Packers |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34697292/new-england-patriots-rule-qb-mac-jones-brian-hoyer-set-start |access-date=October 1, 2022 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Benjamin |first=Cody |date=October 2, 2022 |title=Patriots' Brian Hoyer leaves Week 4 vs. Packers with head injury; rookie Bailey Zappe takes over at QB |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/patriots-brian-hoyer-leaves-week-4-vs-packers-with-head-injury-rookie-bailey-zappe-takes-over-at-qb/ |access-date=August 4, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> He completed 10 of 15 passes for 99 yards and a touchdown in the narrow 27–24 loss in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reiss |first=Mike |date=October 2, 2022 |title=Zappe replaces hurt Hoyer; Pats fall to Pack in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34713456/new-england-patriots-another-qb-brian-hoyer-leaves-head-injury-bailey-zappe-comes-green-bay-packers |access-date=August 4, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Zappe was also the first rookie in the league to throw a touchdown pass that season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reiss |first=Mike |date=October 2, 2022 |title=Patriots rookie QB Bailey Zappe throws first career touchdown pass |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34714250/patriots-rookie-qb-bailey-zappe-throws-first-career-touchdown-pass?platform=amp |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> He made his starting debut the following week against the [[Detroit Lions]], completing 17 of 21 passes for 188 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the 29–0 shutout victory.<ref name="BlanksDetroit">{{Cite web |last=McCarriston |first=Shanna |date=October 9, 2022 |title=Lions vs. Patriots score, takeaways: New England blanks Detroit in rookie Bailey Zappe's first NFL start |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/lions-vs-patriots-score-takeaways-new-england-blanks-detroit-in-rookie-bailey-zappes-first-nfl-start/live/ |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> After a Week 6 victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]], where he threw for 309 yards and two touchdowns, Zappe became the first rookie quarterback in the [[Super Bowl|Super Bowl era]] to win his first two starts and have a passer rating of at least 100 in each start.<ref name="FirstRookie">{{Cite web |last=Goss |first=Nick |date=October 16, 2022 |title=Bailey Zappe becomes first NFL rookie QB ever to achieve this feat |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/patriots/patriots-bailey-zappe-becomes-first-nfl-rookie-qb-achieve-feat |access-date=October 16, 2022 |website=[[NBC Sports]]}}</ref>

While Hoyer was on injured reserve, Jones returned and Zappe was named the backup in the Week 7 ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' matchup against the [[Chicago Bears]]. Zappe relieved a struggling Jones during the second quarter after the latter threw an interception.<ref name="FiveTakeways">{{Cite web |last=Bird |first=Hayden |date=October 25, 2022 |title=5 takeaways from the Patriots' loss to the Bears as the Bailey Zappe vs. Mac Jones debate persists |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/new-england-patriots/2022/10/25/patriot-bears-takeaways-bailey-zappe-mac-jones/ |access-date=October 25, 2022 |website=[[Boston.com]]}}</ref> He threw a touchdown pass on his first drive and led the Patriots to a touchdown on his second, but did not score again and threw two interceptions in the fourth quarter of the 33–14 defeat.<ref name="HotStart">{{Cite web |last=Benjamin |first=Cody |date=October 25, 2022 |title=Patriots bench Mac Jones for Bailey Zappe vs. Bears; rookie QB struggles after hot start in 'MNF' loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/patriots-bench-mac-jones-for-bailey-zappe-vs-bears-rookie-qb-struggles-after-hot-start-in-mnf-loss/ |access-date=October 25, 2022 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> Zappe was retained as the team's backup behind Jones for the remainder of the season, not seeing play again in his rookie season.<ref name="StartSunday">{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2022 |title=Mac Jones will Start Sunday When the Pats Battle the Jets |url=https://nesn.com/bets/2022/10/mac-jones-will-start-sunday-when-the-pats-battle-the-jets/ |access-date=October 29, 2022 |website=[[NESN]]}}</ref>

==== 2023 ====
On August 29, 2023, Zappe was waived by the Patriots as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the team's practice squad the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Patriots waive Bailey Zappe, Malik Cunningham |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/patriots-waive-bailey-zappe-malik-cunningham |access-date=August 29, 2023 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Patriots signing Bailey Zappe, Malik Cunningham to practice squad after QBs clear waivers |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/patriots-signing-bailey-zappe-malik-cunningham-practice-squad-waivers |access-date=August 30, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On September 9, Zappe was signed to the active roster, returning as backup to Jones.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2023 |title=Sources: Pats plan to add Zappe, release Corral |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38359581/sources-patriots-add-bailey-zappe-release-matt-corral |access-date=September 9, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

After making several relief appearances throughout the season, Zappe was named the starter for Week 13 against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] after struggles from Mac Jones.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ryan |first=Conor |title=Bailey Zappe gets start as Patriots QB against Chargers |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/new-england-patriots/2023/12/03/bailey-zappe-gets-start-patriots-quarterback-against-chargers-news/ |access-date=December 11, 2023 |website=www.boston.com |language=en-US}}</ref> The Patriots lost 0–6 as Zappe completed 13 of 25 passes for 141 yards,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goss |first=Nick |date=December 4, 2023 |title=Patriots-Chargers takeaways: Pats offense finds new low in shutout loss |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/patriots-chargers-takeaways-pats-offense-210409956.html |access-date=December 11, 2023 |website=Yahoo! Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> marking Zappe's first career loss as a starter. He started the following game against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], leading New England to a 21–18 upset victory as he passed for 3 touchdowns in the first half.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McElroy |first=Jordy |date=December 8, 2023 |title=Instant analysis: Patriots, Bailey Zappe stun Steelers in 21-18 win on Thursday |url=https://patriotswire.usatoday.com/2023/12/07/instant-analysis-patriots-bailey-zappe-stun-steelers-21-18-win-thursday/ |access-date=December 11, 2023 |website=Patriots Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> After a home loss to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Zappe led the Patriots to a 26–23 win over the [[Denver Broncos]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Graham |first=Pat |date=December 25, 2023 |title=Patriots turn rough start into memorable finish in 26-23 victory over Broncos |url=https://apnews.com/article/patriots-broncos-nfl-score-646dc31ef5ed8dec45a7ecafe33386fe |access-date=January 7, 2024 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> but struggled against the [[Buffalo Bills]] and [[New York Jets]] in the Patriots' final two games of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Magliozzi |first=Connor |date=January 7, 2024 |title=Patriots end season with 17-3 loss to Jets |url=https://www.wabi.tv/2024/01/07/patriots-end-season-with-17-3-loss-jets/ |access-date=January 7, 2024 |website=wabi.tv |language=en}}</ref> In those two games combined, he threw for less than 300 yards, five interceptions and no touchdowns; three of the five interceptions came in the first half of the Bills game alone.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McElroy |first=Jordy |date=December 31, 2023 |title=Twitter reacts to Bailey Zappe throwing three interceptions in first half |url=https://patriotswire.usatoday.com/lists/twitter-reacts-bailey-zappe-throwing-three-interceptions-first-half/ |access-date=January 7, 2024 |website=Patriots Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

On August 26, 2024, Zappe was waived by the Patriots as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Russini |first=Dianna |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Patriots cut Bailey Zappe; Brock Purdy, Skylar Thompson only 2022 QBs still with team that drafted them |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5726614/2024/08/27/bailey-zappe-patriots-release/ |access-date=2024-08-28 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

=== Kansas City Chiefs (first stint) ===
On August 28, 2024, Zappe was signed to the practice squad of the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=August 28, 2024 |title=Chiefs to sign ex-Patriots starting QB Bailey Zappe to practice squad |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chiefs-to-sign-ex-patriots-starting-qb-bailey-zappe-to-practice-squad |access-date=2024-08-28 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
