'''Badara Traore''' (born March 12, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] at [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Badara Traore College Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/badara-traore-1.html|access-date=2021-05-03|website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Kubena|first=Brooks|title=The story of Badara Traore: his family's 'American Dream,' long train rides and long journeys|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_3013d3b2-9204-11e9-87ed-5b6671577577.html|access-date=2021-05-03|website=The Advocate|date=22 June 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Traore was born to Bakary Traore and Rouguiatou Kaba, both African immigrants, and grew up in [[Hyde Park, Boston|Hyde Park, Massachusetts]]. He attended [[Matignon High School]], where he played on the football and basketball teams and commuted two hours each way.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Conte|first=J. D.|title=Suffolk security officer reflects on son's national title at LSU, possible NFL future|url=https://thesuffolkjournal.com/28349/sports/suffolk-security-officer-reflects-on-sons-national-title-at-lsu-possible-nfl-future/|access-date=2021-05-05|website=The Suffolk Journal}}</ref>

== College career ==
Traore played two seasons at [[ASA College]] in [[Brooklyn|Brooklyn, New York]]. In 2018, he transferred to [[Louisiana State University]] to continue his collegiate football career, turning down offers from 26 schools, including Oklahoma, Auburn, and Texas.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Badara Traore, 2018 Offensive tackle - Rivals.com|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2018/badara-traore-72495#school-interests|access-date=2021-05-02|website=n.rivals.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Badara Traore's path to the NFL filled with obstacles|url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/Article/Badara-Traores-path-to-the-NFL-filled-with-obstacles-LSU-146233540/|access-date=2021-05-03|website=Geaux247|language=en-US}}</ref> In his first season at LSU, he played in all 13 games, starting 2 of them, and was referred to as "one of the most improved players on the team" by head coach [[Ed Orgeron]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=In Focus: Badara Traore|url=https://lsusports.net/news/2019/11/22/in-focus-badara-traore.aspx|access-date=2021-05-02|website=LSU Tigers| date=22 November 2019 |language=en}}</ref> Going into his senior year, Traore served as the backup right tackle to Austin Deculus and took snaps on special teams. During his final season at LSU, he played in 13 games and earned 3 starts against Georgia Southern, Ole Miss, and Arkansas (one at left tackle and two at right tackle).

On August 25, 2021, Traore was claimed off waivers by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Official: Jaguars Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-jaguars-make-roster-moves|website=Jaguars.com|date=August 25, 2021|access-date=August 26, 2021|archive-date=August 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210826053032/https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-jaguars-make-roster-moves|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2021, and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Jaguars Reduce Roster to 53|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-reduce-roster-to-53|website=Jaguars.com|date=August 31, 2021|access-date=September 2, 2021|archive-date=September 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210902030149/https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-reduce-roster-to-53|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Official: Jaguars claim Johnson, sign 13 players to practice squad|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-jaguars-claim-johnson-sign-13-players-to-practice-squad|author=Oehser, John|website=Jaguars.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref> Traore made his NFL debut on January 9, 2022, against the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TraoBa00/gamelog/2021/ | title=Badara Traore 2021 Game Log | website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] }}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 10, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Jaguars sign 8 players to Reserve/Future contracts|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-sign-8-players-to-reserve-future-contracts|website=Jaguars.com|date=January 10, 2022}}</ref>

On August 29, 2022, Traore was waived by the Jaguars.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Jaguars release four, waive six ahead of the 53-man roster deadline on August 30, 2022|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-release-four-waive-six-ahead-of-the-53-man-deadline-on-augu|website=Jaguars.com|date=August 29, 2022}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On September 1, 2022, Traore was signed to the [[Arizona Cardinals]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Re-Sign Aaron Brewer; Place Antonio Hamilton On NFI|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-re-signs-aaron-brewer-adds-devon-kennard-to-practice-squad|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardianls.com|date=September 1, 2022}}</ref> On October 29, 2022, he was elevated to the active roster.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-29 |title=Arizona Cardinals elevate DT Woods, OL Traore from practice squad |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3354242/arizona-cardinals-elevate-dt-woods-ol-traore-from-practice-squad/ |access-date=2022-10-31 |website=Arizona Sports |language=en}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 11, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bernhard Seikovits Among 14 'Futures' Cardinals Sign For 2023|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/bernhard-seikovits-among-14-futures-cardinals-sign-for-2023|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=January 11, 2023}}</ref> On August 29, 2023, Traore was released by the Cardinals as part of final roster cuts before the start of the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite web|title= Cardinals Make Moves To Get To 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/arizona-cardinals-make-moves-to-get-to-53-man-roster|website=AZCardinals.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On December 18, 2023, Traore signed a letter of intent to join the [[DC Defenders]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] for the upcoming 2024 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=XFL Transactions |url=https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=www.xfl.com |language=en |archive-date=March 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200316152142/https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |url-status=dead }}</ref> The next day, Traore was signed to the [[Carolina Panthers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rizzutti |first1=Anthony |title=Panthers sign offensive lineman to practice squad on Tuesday |url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2023/12/19/panthers-sign-offensive-lineman-practice-squad-badara-traore-bears-jaguars-cardinals-xfl/ |website=Panthers Wire |access-date=20 December 2023}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 8, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers extend three, sign 11 practice squaders to future deals|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-extend-three-sign-11-practice-squaders-to-future-deals|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=January 8, 2024}}</ref> He was waived/injured on August 22.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign former Tennessee linebacker|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-sign-former-tennessee-linebacker|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=August 22, 2024}}</ref>

Traore was waived by the Panthers with an injury settlement on August 22, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gantt |first1=Darin |title=Panthers sign former Tennessee linebacker |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-sign-former-tennessee-linebacker |website=panthers.com |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref>

'''Zonovan''' "'''Bam'''" '''Knight''' (born April 11, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] and [[kickoff returner]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State Wolfpack]].

==Early life==
Knight attended [[Southern Nash High School]] in [[Bailey, North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stout |first=Jon |date=January 17, 2018 |title=Recruitment ramping up for Southern Nash's Zonovan Knight |url=https://www.highschoolot.com/recruitment-ramping-up-for-southern-nash-s-zonovan-knight/17267349/ |access-date=February 2, 2023 |website=High School OT |language=en}}</ref> During his high school career, he had a school record 5,073 rushing yards and 71 [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=David |date=August 5, 2021 |title=How did NC State football RB Zonovan 'Bam' Knight get his nickname? It's a cute story |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/2021/08/05/how-did-nc-state-football-running-back-zonovan-bam-knight-get-his-nickname/5501230001/ |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=The Fayetteville Observer}}</ref> He committed to [[North Carolina State University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=R. Cory |date=July 9, 2018 |title=Top NC RB Zonovan Knight commits to NC State for 2019 class |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina-state/article/top-nc-rb-zonovan-knight-commits-to-nc-state-wolfpack-for-2019-f-119061940/ |access-date=May 25, 2023 |website=247Sports |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2018 |title=Southern Nash standout RB Zonovan Knight commits to NC State |url=https://www.highschoolot.com/southern-nash-standout-rb-zonovan-knight-commits-to-/17685118/ |access-date=May 25, 2023 |website=High School OT |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman at NC State in [[2019 NC State Wolfpack football team|2019]], Knight started seven games and led the team with 745 yards on 136 carries with five touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Durham |first=Paul |date=September 17, 2020 |title=Former Firebird ready for more: 'Bam' Knight takes field after breakout rookie season at NC State |url=https://southernnashnews.com/former-firebird-ready-for-more-bam-knight-takes-field-after-breakout-roo-p2290-163.htm |access-date=May 25, 2023 |website=Southern Nash News}}</ref> In [[2020 NC State Wolfpack football team|2020]], he again led the team with 788 yards on 143 carries with 10 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pope IV |first=Jonas |date=July 27, 2021 |title=N.C. State's Bam Knight is healthy, and motivated, which is good news for the Wolfpack |url=https://greensboro.com/sports/n-c-states-bam-knight-is-healthy-and-motivated-which-is-good-news-for-the/article_234ef379-ce47-5911-bc2f-d37e72e751c1.html |access-date=May 25, 2023 |website=Greensboro News and Record}}</ref> He returned to NC State as the starter in [[2021 NC State Wolfpack football team|2021]].

===New York Jets===
Knight signed with the [[New York Jets]] as an undrafted free agent on May 6, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Sam |date=May 6, 2022 |title=Jets Sign 5 Undrafted Free Agents |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2022/05/jets-sign-5-undrafted-free-agents |access-date=May 25, 2023 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref> He made the Jets' initial 53-man roster on August 30.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lange |first=Randy |last2=Greenberg |first2=Ethan |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Final Cuts: Jets Move 27 Players to Trim Roster to NFL's 53-Man Limit |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-53-man-roster-2022-season |access-date=May 25, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> Knight was waived by New York on September 5.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Butchko |first=John |date=September 5, 2022 |title=Jets Bring Back Conor McDermott; Waive Zonovan Knight |url=https://www.ganggreennation.com/2022/9/5/23338410/jets-bring-back-conor-mcdermott-waive-zonovan-knight |access-date=May 25, 2023 |website=Gang Green Nation |language=en}}</ref> He was re-signed to the team's [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=September 6, 2022 |title=Jets Sign 3 Players to Practice Squad |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-3-players-to-practice-squad-x3106 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> Knight was promoted to the active roster on October 25.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=October 25, 2022 |title=Jets Place RB Breece Hall and OL Alijah Vera-Tucker on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-breece-hall-and-alijah-vera-tucker-injured-reserve-sign-zonovan-knight |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> Knight made his NFL debut on November 27 against the [[2022 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], where he set a new franchise record with 103 yards from scrimmage in his debut, including 69 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodman |first=Max |date=November 27, 2022 |title=Jets' Rookie Helps to Revive Run Game With Historic Debut |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jets/news/new-york-jets-rookie-zonovan-knight-revives-running-game-nfl-debut-against-chicago-bears |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=Jets Nation |publisher=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> 

Knight was waived by the Jets as part of final roster cuts on August 28, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ehalt |first=Matt |date=August 28, 2023 |title=Jets cut Zonovan ‘Bam’ Knight in Dalvin Cook roster casualty |url=https://nypost.com/2023/08/28/jets-cut-zonovan-knight-as-53-man-roster-takes-shape/ |access-date=August 30, 2023 |website=New York Post}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On August 30, 2023, Knight was signed to the [[Detroit Lions]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Raven |first=Benjamin |date=August 31, 2023 |title=Lions add kicker Michael Badgley, running back Zonovan Knight to practice squad |url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2023/08/detroit-lions-add-kicker-michael-badgley-to-practice-squad-after-trade-rumors.html |access-date=August 30, 2023 |website=Michigan Live}}</ref> On September 19, Knight was signed to the active roster.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Logan |date=September 19, 2023 |title=Lions Promoting RB Zonovan Knight To Active Roster |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/lions-promoting-rb-zonovan-knight-to-active-roster/ |access-date=September 19, 2023 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on October 14.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2023 |title=Lions' Zonovan Knight: Moved to IR |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/lions-zonovan-knight-moved-to-ir/ |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

On August 27, 2024, Knight was released by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions announce roster moves|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/detroit-lions-announce-roster-moves-nfl-53-man|website=DetroitLions.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref>

===New York Jets (second stint)===
On November 26, 2024, Knight was signed to the New York Jets' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign RB Zonovan Knight and WR Easop Winston Jr. to Practice Squad|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-easop-winston-jr-and-bam-knight-practice-squad-11-26-2024|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=November 26, 2024}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On January 7, 2025, Knight signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Ink Futures Deal With Four More Players|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-ink-futures-deal-with-four-more-players|author=Gershman, Zach|website=AZCardinals.com|date=January 7, 2025}}</ref> On August 26, he made the Cardinals' initial 53-man roster as a kick returner. Following injuries to [[James Conner (American football)|James Conner]], [[Trey Benson]], and [[Emari Demercado]], Knight stepped in as the number one running back on the team. On December 16, Knight was placed on [[Injured reserve list|injured reserve]] due to a season-ending ankle injury suffered in Week 15 against the [[2025 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Drake |first=Tyler |date=2025-12-16 |title=Cardinals place RB Bam Knight on injured reserve |url=https://arizonasports.com/nfl/arizona-cardinals/rb-bam-knight-ir/3605808/ |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=Arizona Sports |language=en}}</ref> He finished the season with 269 rushing yards and four touchdowns through 12 games and eight starts.

On March 12, 2026, Knight re-signed with the Cardinals on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gershman |first1=Zach |title=Bam Knight, Starling Thomas V Agree To Return With Cardinals |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/starling-thomas-v-bam-knight-agree-to-return-with-cardinals |website=Azcardinals.com |access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Barrington Wade''' (born March 16, 1998) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]]  [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]].

==College career==
Wade was a member of the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]] for five seasons, redshirting as a true freshman. He finished his collegiate career with 23 tackles, one sack, 1.5 tackles for loss and two interceptions in 33 games played.<ref name=officially/>

'''Bailey Gaither''' (born January 11, 1997) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] at [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State]].

== Early life ==
Gaither attended [[Paso Robles High School]] as a two-sport athlete, also excelling in baseball.

As a senior for the Bearcats, Gaither caught 73 passes for 1,480 yards,<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 5, 2015 |title=College Football Signings – San Jose State |pages=4C |work=The San Jose Mercury News}}</ref> returned 16 kickoffs for a 44.6-yard per-return average, and scored 30 total touchdowns on the season, as PRHS won the [[CIF Southern Section]] Northern Division championship.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jankowski |first=Alex J. |date=January 11, 2015 |title=Shining Bright – Tribune County Football Player of the Year: Paso Robles' Bailey Gaither |pages=S1 |work=The Tribune (San Luis Obispo, CA)}}</ref>

Gaither, who scored 56 combined touchdowns in his prep career, was evaluated as a three-star prospect by the [[247Sports|247 Sports Network]], which ranked him among the top 150 overall players in the state.

He was also a high school teammate of fellow future pro [[Josh Oliver]].

==College career==
After graduating high school, Gaither enrolled at [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State]], where in his first year he redshirted.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://sjsuspartans.com/sports/football/roster/bailey-gaither/4990|title= 84 – Bailey Gaither|website=sjsuspartans.com}}</ref>

Gaither had arguably his best college season in 2019. He started all 12 games and caught 52 passes for 812 yards and 6 touchdowns (in six consecutive games, setting a program record<ref>{{Cite book |title=San Jose State Football Record Book: Offerpad Arizona Bowl edition |publisher=SJSU Athletics Department |year=2022 |pages=39 |language=English}}</ref>). He also recorded 1 punt return for 10 yards and had a blocked punt that was featured on ESPN [[SportsCenter]]'s Top 10 "Plays of the Day" for October 26.<ref name="auto1" />

In his final college season, Gaither earned first-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] selection<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Nick |date=May 4, 2021 |title=NFL – Former Paso Robles, San Jose State standout signs with Packers |pages=1B |work=San Luis Obispo Tribune}}</ref> and graduated with his bachelor's degree in communication studies. He started 7 of 7 games as a captain for the Spartans, and caught 41 passes for 725 yards and 4 touchdowns. He also had 5 punt returns for 37 yards.

During the 2020 season, he helped SJSU earn its first AP Top 25 Poll ranking in eight years, as the Spartans peaked at No. 19 before finishing 24th in the final poll.

'''Barrett Carter''' (born October 23, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the Bengals in the fourth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Carter was born on October 23, 2002. He attended [[North Gwinnett High School]]; he recorded 73 tackles and 10 sacks in 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article241223396.html|title=Football recruit Barrett Carter likes what he sees in Clemson|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|date=March 16, 2020}}</ref> Carter was rated a four-star recruit and committed to play college football at Clemson over offers from Georgia, Auburn, and Ohio State.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/clemson-football-recruiting-four-star-linebacker-barrett-carter-commits-to-tigers/|title=Clemson football recruiting: Four-star linebacker Barrett Carter commits to Tigers|first=Barrett|last=Sallee|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=May 21, 2020|access-date=October 15, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
Carter played in 12 games as a freshman in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/picture-gallery/sports/college/clemson/2022/08/21/barrett-carter-clemson-football-linebacker-photos/7858625001/|title=Barrett Carter: Clemson football linebacker through the years|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=October 6, 2022|access-date=October 15, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article264421756.html|title=5 breakout players to know for Clemson's 2022 defense|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|date=August 13, 2022|access-date=October 15, 2022}}</ref> He entered his sophomore season as a starter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/clemson/football/clemson-lb-barrett-carter-thinks-opener-against-georgia-tech-a-statement-game|title=Clemson LB Barrett Carter Thinks Opener Against Georgia Tech 'A Statement Game'|first=JP|last=Priester|website=[[SI.com]]|date=September 6, 2022|access-date=October 15, 2022}}</ref>

'''Barron Dean Bowman''' (born December 18, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]] for one season with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech]]. He was also a member of the [[Los Angeles Rams]].

==Early life and college==
Barron Dean Bowman was born on December 18, 1964, in [[Port Arthur, Texas]].<ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/b/bowm00200.html | title=Barry Bowman | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Spring Hill High School (Texas)|Spring Hill High]] in [[Longview, Texas]].<ref name="pfa"/>

He was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]] of [[Louisiana Tech University]] from 1983 to 1986.<ref name="pfa"/>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1987 NFL draft]], Bowman signed with the [[Los Angeles Rams]] on May 1.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/bowm00200.html | title=Barry Bowman NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He was traded to the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on August 25, 1987.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on September 8.<ref name="transactions"/> He was later re-signed by the Seahawks on October 14, during the [[1987 NFL players strike]].<ref name="transactions"/> Bowman played in one game for the Seahawks, punting three times for 104 yards in a 37–14 victory over the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BowmBa20/gamelog/1987/ | title=Barry Bowman | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He was released by the Seahawks on October 20, 1987, after the strike ended.<ref name="transactions"/>

==Coaching career==
Bowman has spent over 30 years as a [[high school football]] coach.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://winknews.com/2020/11/30/new-cape-coral-hs-head-football-coach-has-record-of-success/ | title=New Cape Coral HS head football coach has record of success | publisher=winknews.com | date=November 30, 2020 | accessdate=24 December 2024 | author=Shaw, Derrick}}</ref> He won three consecutive state titles at [[Daingerfield High School]] from 2008 to 2010.<ref name="A">{{cite web | url=https://cbc-radio.com/local-news-blog/128676 | title=Center ISD hires Barry Bowman to be athletic director/head football coach | publisher=cbc-radio.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.smoaky.com/news/view-modern.php?ArticleID=3178 | title=Barry Bowman to be D.C. at Pine Tree | publisher=smoaky.com | date=May 1, 2013 | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He has also coached high school [[track and field|track]].<ref name="A"/>

'''Barry L. Cantrell II''' (born November 2, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Punter (American football)|punter]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Fordham Rams football|Fordham Rams]]. He was signed as an undrafted free agent by the NFL's [[Philadelphia Eagles]].

He also played for the [[Frankfurt Galaxy (NFL Europe)|Frankfurt Galaxy]] of [[NFL Europe]] and the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the NFL.

==College career==
While at Fordham, Cantrell earned Academic All-American honors as well as being named the [[Patriot League]] Scholar Athlete of the Year in football in 1996 and 1997.<ref name="Legend">{{cite web |url=https://fordhamsports.com/news/2020/3/25/football-ram-legend-barry-cantrell.aspx |title=Ram Legend: Barry Cantrell |website=FordhamSports.com |date=March 25, 2020 |access-date=February 24, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Anniversary">{{cite web |url=https://fordhamsports.com/news/2011/7/25/072511aaa_100.aspx?path=tickets |title=Three Football Rams Named to Patriot League 25th Anniversary Team |website=FordhamSports.com |date=July 25, 2011 |access-date=February 24, 2024}}</ref>

===Football===
In 1997, as a senior, he was named [[Associated Press]] First-team All-American when he set a school record of 45.8 yards-per-punt average, which also let [[NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision|NCAA I-AA]]. He also set a school record in yards (2,890), which stood for eight years, before being broken by Anthony DiFino.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fordhamsports.com/news/2005/11/23/112305aaa_879.aspx?print=true |title=Six Fordham University Football Rams Named All-Patriot League |website=FordhamSports.com |date=November 23, 2005 |access-date=February 24, 2024}}</ref> He was also named First-team [[Burger King]] All-American and Second-team All-American by the [[The Sports Network (wire service)|Sports Network]]. When he graduated, he held numerous school records including career punts (267), career punting yardage (10,649), and career average (39.9). He also held the Patriot League record for season and career averages.<ref name="Legend"/><ref name="Anniversary" />

In 2001, he was named to the Patriot League 15th Anniversary team, and in 2011 to the 25th Anniversary team.<ref name="Anniversary" />

===Track and field===
As a senior, Cantrell won the 1998 [[Atlantic 10]] Indoor Championships high jump competition, as well as recording a meet record jump of 7' 1.75", a still standing record (as of March 25, 2020). He also earned 1998 Indoor All-American honors by finishing 11th at the NCAA National Championships.<ref name="Legend"/><ref name="Anniversary" />

==Professional career==
Cantrell when undrafted in the [[1998 NFL draft]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was then assigned to the [[Frankfurt Galaxy (NFL Europe)|Frankfurt Galaxy]] of [[NFL Europe]]. While playing for the Galaxy, he punted 39 times, for 1,602 yards, with an average of 41.1 yards, and a long of 58 yards. He helped the team finish 6-4 and win the [[World Bowl '99|World Bowl]] championship. He then joined the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in [[2000 Dallas Cowboys season|2000]] and appeared in two games.

==Personal life==
After leaving football, Cantrell returned to Florida and served as a [[financial advisor]] for Bernstein Investment Research & Management, before moving on to become the director of financial planning for [[Edelman Financial Engines]].<ref name="Anniversary" /><ref name="Legend"/>

'''Barry Glen Pettyjohn''' (born March 29, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|tackle]] for the [[Houston Oilers]] of [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PettBa20.htm | title=Barry Pettyjohn stats |access-date=February 24, 2025 |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Barry Pettyjohn, T |url= https://www.nfl.com/players/barry-pettyjohn/ |access-date=February 24, 2025 |work=Nfl.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-pittsburgh-press/166580777/|newspaper=[[The Pittsburgh Press]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 15, 1984|page=54|title=The successor|author=Molinari, Dave}} {{Open access}}</ref> He later was a football coach.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-cincinnati-enquirer/166580951/|newspaper=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 19, 2008|page=46|title=A cautionary tale}} {{Open access}}</ref>
